body:
## Summary

Applies the shared _has_consolidated_label predicate at the pre-ranking candidate filter so consolidated issues that the dispatch management-label gate always rejects no longer cost a full 12-21s dispatch_with_dedup attempt every cycle. Changes: (1) pulse-repo-meta.sh candidate projection keeps .body for consolidated issues when the snapshot carries it; (2) _has_consolidated_label accepts both GitHub label objects and normalized string labels and defaults the auto-dispatch label under set -u; (3) new _dispatch_filter_consolidated_candidates, chained from the existing _dispatch_filter_capability_cooled_candidates entrypoint, drops always-rejected consolidated candidates, logs one summary line per repo enumeration, and does at most 5 bounded REST body reads for consolidated+auto-dispatch candidates without a body (fail-open on any read error); (4) for excluded consolidated issues without auto-dispatch that have an open draft PR checkpoint, posts one idempotent trusted CONSOLIDATED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION comment per draft head (runner-local 6h lookup stamp, max 3 lookups per pass). It never re-adds auto-dispatch or changes labels, assignees, PR state, trust, continuation or dispatch authority; the dispatch-time gate remains as defense-in-depth. title: GH#35078: fix incremental recovery archives with exact base and staged state
body:
## Summary

For #35078. Restore the existing incremental recovery model instead of requiring a full-history bundle for Git metadata preservation.

- Record the exact fork/base SHA; derive a unique merge-base from the selected integration branch when no explicit SHA is supplied.
- Keep separate staged and unstaged binary patches and the existing untracked/ignored payload.
- Preserve Git administration, FETCH_HEAD dependencies, private refs, reflogs and index-only/resolve-undo objects without bundling objects already covered by the base. A clean copy with no extra dependencies has no commits.bundle.
- Verify using only the recorded base graph plus archive data, not unrelated objects in the original repository. Restore metadata into a separate repository without changing existing source branches or using alternates.
- Make legacy migration use the incremental mode. Retain compatibility with explicitly requested self-contained archives; no shared-base store or new archive format.
- Keep fingerprint collection read-only, including disabling Git's automatic diff index refresh.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`: base selection, capture, verification and restore routing.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_snapshot.py`: incremental object selection and base-plus-delta verification/restoration.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_administration.py` and `worktree_archive_readiness.py`: bounded preservation of known metadata.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_recovery_migrate.py`: reuse the existing incremental archive path.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`: extend existing archive, migration and retirement fixtures.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.md` and `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`: document exact-base dependency and preservation semantics.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified.
- Real-data pilot: all 9,819 files and Git administration matched the original full snapshot after restoration from the recorded base plus incremental artifacts. No alternates; original source unchanged.
- Allocated archive size: **2,596,864 bytes**, versus **250,548,224 bytes** for the rejected full-history prototype and **515,612,672 bytes** for the original recovery bucket. Both patches are empty for this clean sample; commits.bundle is absent. Metadata accounts for most remaining archive size.
- New fixtures verify distinct staged/unstaged versions, index-only blobs, historical/private/FETCH_HEAD objects, no bundle for a clean copy, moving base branches, and refusal when the base becomes unavailable.
- A 28-scenario archive/migration/retirement run passed 27 scenarios; the remaining test had assumed every archive contains a bundle. Its assertion now compares the complete artifact path inventory to prove no second capture is allocated, and its focused rerun passed.
- After the final restore-routing refactor: all 8 existing shell archive tests and 3 focused incremental/full restore tests passed. Changed-file local gates, including ShellCheck and complexity checks, passed.
- Operator-approved cleanup removed both pilot directories, their test restores, and the earlier incomplete capture artifacts only after verification. The original recovery bucket and its source fingerprint remain unchanged; a cleanup receipt is retained with the reservation.

## Safety and scope

The existing common repository must retain the recorded base commit for the archive's lifetime. Missing base evidence blocks metadata verification, restore and retirement. This is an explicit dependency, not a claim that an incremental archive is independently portable.

No automatic retirement, producer switch, archive expiry, or new storage system is introduced. Unknown metadata and unsupported file permissions still fail closed. The parent issue remains open.

title: GH#35129: apply repo-declared queue recovery policy
body:
## Summary

Resolves #35129

A repo can now declare its own queue-recovery policy, and the pulse terminal-blocker / integration-recovery supervisor treats the actions it enables as maintainer-delegated authority.

- **Schema**: `.aidevops.json` gains the optional key `recovery_policy: "path.md#Exact heading"` (`.agents/configs/aidevops-config.schema.json`).
- **Loader** `.agents/scripts/recovery-policy-helper.sh <owner/repo>`: read-only. It checks write/maintain/admin access, then reads `.aidevops.json` and the policy document at **one pinned default-branch commit** through the contents API. It never reads managed repo directories. Exit `0` returns validated JSON, `3` means no policy is declared and `1` means the policy is invalid or unavailable (fail closed). Validation rules:
  - Only `outlier_hold`, `session_cap_split` and `brief_authority` are accepted. Each needs conditions, a template and labels.
  - `outlier_hold` must keep `hold-for-review`. `session_cap_split` needs a positive `session_budget` and a `split_pattern`.
  - Lifecycle, origin and trust labels are rejected, compared case-insensitively.
  - The parser is fence-aware: headings and `json` blocks nested inside another code fence don't count.
  - Path traversal is refused.
- **Cross-runner intake** (`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`): when the repo policy enables at least one action, `seed` also queues circuits that another runner opened. Those circuits must come from an OWNER or MEMBER, which matches the circuit library's trust rule, so a foreign bare-COLLABORATOR circuit is never queued. These entries are marked `intake: policy_remote` and have empty `local_excerpts`, so only public evidence is used. `pending` retires them once the policy stops enabling an action. Without a policy, intake is unchanged.
- **Supervisor contract**: the `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh` prompt and `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Terminal-blocker recovery" point to the new `reference/recovery-policy.md`. That reference covers:
  - the per-action rules: chain hold with dependant repoints, session-cap split, pre-authorized brief repair;
  - deduplication through public markers;
  - wake mapping: holds use `human_decision`, splits and repoints use `dependency_change`, brief repairs use `brief_revision`;
  - the safety rules that stay in force: no credentials, permissions, spending, data imports, record merges or publication.

## Continuation note

This continues the released worker draft (head `7a66dd5`). Its final local commit was never pushed. Review of the checkpoint found and fixed these problems:

- GitHub's contents API wraps base64 at 60 columns, and jq `@base64d` rejects it. The loader could never have read a real policy.
- Cross-runner seeding accepted COLLABORATOR circuits that `_tbr_check_entry` then silently dropped.
- Remote entries leaked same-number local excerpts.
- "No policy" and "error" were indistinguishable.
- Markdown parsing mishandled nested and example fences.

The missing `tests/test-recovery-policy.sh` is added.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`: 29 passed, 0 failed. GitHub is mocked and nothing is written to the network. It covers:
  - no policy (exit 3, intake unchanged);
  - an enabled `outlier_hold` loaded with both reads pinned to one revision;
  - unlisted actions not returned;
  - fail-closed cases: read-only access, unknown action, missing hold label, protected and mixed-case labels, invalid JSON, duplicate heading, two blocks, nested example fences, path traversal;
  - cross-runner seed and pending end to end;
  - `record` wake values;
  - the supervisor prompt contract.
- `tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: 35 passed. `tests/test-pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh`: 50 passed.
- ShellCheck is clean on all touched shell files. `markdownlint-cli2` is clean on the touched docs. The schema is valid JSON.
- Live read-only run: `recovery-policy-helper.sh marcusquinn/aidevops` exits `3` because this repo has no `.aidevops.json`.
- Independent review found two issues: case-insensitive label bypass and nested-fence policy injection. Both are fixed and covered by regression tests.

## Runtime Testing

`self-assessed`, plus mocked runtime paths. The loader was run once read-only against the live GitHub API. Applying hold, split or repair actions is supervisor AI judgment, not deterministic code. The issue's scope note keeps policy judgment in the supervisor, so no live issue chain was mutated for testing.

title: GH#35172: Git-only recovery capture with shared worktree restoration
body:
## Summary

Resolves #35172.

- New producer/migration receipts use explicit Git-only capture: exact HEAD/base, incremental commits and separate staged/unstaged binary patches. Untracked/ignored content and raw Git administration are intentionally outside this contract; there are no project-specific exclusions.
- Capture returns `archived`, not `verified`, without verification, trial restoration or repeated whole-tree hashing. Existing receipts retain their original preservation policy. Integrity, source-drift, ownership and removal guards remain outside capture.
- Git-only restoration imports saved commits and calls `worktree-helper.sh add`, the same creation/registration entrypoint used by Pulse, before the existing staged/unstaged patch application.
- Add private, correlated stage timings and a read-only report. Logging is best effort, never removal evidence.

## Scope and reference pattern

Changes are confined to the worktree archive helper/snapshot/restore, recovery producer/migration/retirement policy transitions, timing module, recovery docs and one focused case in the existing archive lifecycle fixture. Existing legacy profile recovery assertions explicitly select `preserve-v1` to continue testing their original full-preservation contract. Pulse's existing `worktree-helper.sh add` usage is the creation API reference; no Pulse worker execution or new test infrastructure is introduced.

The shared Git repository must retain the recorded base. Unmerged and intent-to-add index states fail closed. Patch formatting explicitly overrides color and path-prefix preferences. Capture does not replace a quiescence requirement or authorize deleting a source.

## Verification

title: GH#35186: fix: replay verbatim user input and images after compaction
body:
## Summary

Resolves #35186

In long-running OpenCode 1.x sessions, images the user attached, the aim of each user turn, and the user's instructions, including authorisations, are lost, paraphrased or ignored after compaction. This PR finds the causes and fixes them in the aidevops plugin, without host patches.

### Root causes (OpenCode v1.19.3 `packages/opencode/src/session/`)

1. `compaction.ts` `serialize()` replaces every user file part with `[Attached image/png: <name>]`, so the summarizer never sees the media.
2. `message-v2.ts` `filterCompacted()` sends only the compaction pair and a small retained tail. The original user messages and their images stay in the store but are not sent again.
3. `select()`/`splitTurn()` keeps a large turn only from `turn.start + 1`, so the current turn's user message is usually summarized rather than kept.
4. Authorisations then exist only as an assistant-voice paraphrase that is re-summarized on every compaction.
5. aidevops rules ("a summary never widens … authority", "Historical commands are evidence, not authorization") correctly discount that paraphrase. The resumed agent has no user-attributed record, so it asks again.

### Changes

- **NEW** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/compaction-pinned-input.mjs` (hook), `compaction-replay-collect.mjs` (anchor and turn collection) and `compaction-replay-budget.mjs` (budget and part building). When a request starts with a completed compaction summary, the hook reads the session's stored messages once per compaction. It prepends every hidden user turn, in full, plus the most recent inline images/PDFs to the compaction anchor message, so they appear before the summary with a provenance header.
  - Excludes synthetic, ignored, compaction, subtask and tool content.
  - Every turn's aim is kept in full. Within the 64K-character budget every turn is verbatim. Over budget, only the longest messages (pastes) are cut to one shared cap, keeping head and tail with a marker; short turns are never cut. Whole turns are elided only when even 1,500-character excerpts cannot fit, which prevents a compaction loop. Up to 4 media items are replayed. Configurable via env vars.
  - No media replay after an overflow compaction.
  - Cached per summary ID, so the prompt-cache prefix stays byte-stable.
  - Fails open on fetch errors or timeout.
- `index.mjs`: runs the replay first in `messagesTransformHook`.
- `compaction.mjs` summary rules:
  - every aim is quoted verbatim and in full and carried forward unchanged, never paraphrased (long pastes are quoted as marked excerpts). Previously only short aims were quoted and longer ones were paraphrased;
  - authorisations are recorded with their exact scope;
  - attachments are described from conversation evidence only;
  - authority comes from the user's own words (live or replayed), never from the summary;
  - the resume instruction says replayed authorisations stay in force within scope.
- `reference/session.md`: documents the behaviour, budgets and opt-out.

## Verification

- `npm test --prefix .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops`: 1179 tests, 1172 pass, 0 fail, 7 skipped. This includes the existing `test-compaction-checkpoint-scope.mjs` assertions on summary-rule wording.
- Ran `createCompactionInputReplay().inject()` directly on synthetic compacted sessions. Results:
  - authorisation text and the image are replayed before the compaction part;
  - synthetic "Continue…" and synthetic file bodies are excluded;
  - the visible tail is not duplicated;
  - a non-media file is labelled with its path;
  - history is fetched once and part IDs are byte-stable across turns;
  - a second injection is a no-op;
  - an overflow compaction drops media;
  - a request with no compaction is a no-op with no fetch;
  - a fetch error leaves the request unchanged;
  - with 40 messages, the budget keeps the first and newest messages, adds an elision marker, and keeps 2 of 40 images.
  - 30 aim turns plus one 160K-character log paste: all 30 aims are byte-identical in the replay, the paste keeps its leading request and trailing "and then release it", there is one excerpt marker and nothing is elided.
- `qlty smells` (local 0.643) on all new and changed plugin modules: no smells. The first push failed the Qlty smell-regression gate; this push splits the module to fix that.
- `node --check` on all changed modules; `markdownlint-cli2` on `reference/session.md`: 0 issues.
- Not yet observed in a live session. After deploy: paste a screenshot, grant an authorisation, run `/compact`, then ask what the screenshot showed and whether merge is authorised. `~/.aidevops/logs` quality log should show `[compaction-replay] prepared …`.

## Scope notes

- OpenCode 2 (`v2.mjs`) and Claude Code have no equivalent replay yet. Follow-up issue to be filed.
- Found during this work: `quality-hooks-image.mjs` `applyImageSizeGuard` expects provider-shape `{role, content[]}`, but V1 `messages.transform` passes `{info, parts}`, so the guard never runs. Follow-up issue to be filed.

title: GH#35198: harden compaction replay boundaries and resource budgets
body:
## Summary

Resolves #35198.

- Add fresh 128-bit nonces to shared OpenCode 1/2 and Claude Code replay boundaries.
- Account for rendered overhead, notes and fallback attachment labels; zero and tiny budgets emit no turns.
- Cap V2 session prompt retention, keeping the initiating turn and newest turns.

## Files and verification

Production changes are confined to the shared `compaction-replay-budget.mjs`, Claude hook `compaction_user_input_replay.py`, and `compaction-replay-v2-store.mjs`. Regression cases extend the existing `test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs` suite.

## Runtime Testing

- runtime-verified: Node 24.21.0 adapter and compaction suites: all 35 passed, no skips after locked local dependency preparation.
- Synthetic cases exercise literal pasted boundaries, 500 attachment-only turns, budgets 0/1000/2000/4000/64000, Python parity, oversized store pastes and first-plus-newest retention.
- Node syntax and Python py_compile pass.
- Full package `npm test`: 1163 passed, 23 failed, one skipped. All 35 affected adapter/compaction cases passed. Unrelated unchanged fixtures fail on hard-coded `/usr/bin/git` and `/usr/bin/ssh-keygen` paths absent on this runner, a Python-path assertion expecting `/usr/bin/python3`, and a missing Playwright fixture artifact (`page.yml`). The MCP fixture imports MCP configuration/activation modules, not replay code; none of these failing fixtures or production modules are modified here. These failures are not repaired within #35198.
- Repository pre-push `bun run typecheck` passes after frozen-lockfile dependency setup.
- Qlty is unavailable on PATH and in the worktree-local environment; repository `qlty-regression.yml` covers static smells.
- The first merge attempt exposed a Qlty `return-statements` regression in `build_context()`. The disabled and zero-budget guards now share one return, restoring the original five-return count without changing behavior. All 35 scoped tests and Python compilation pass again after this repair; the repaired head awaits fresh CI.

## Decisions

Reserve 1536 characters for the replay envelope, with conservative per-turn rendering costs. A 1000-character budget emits no turns, including with 500 attachment-only turns. Media bytes are governed separately by the existing media limit. V2 prompt text/metadata retention uses a 1000000 JSON-serialized-character and 1000-turn cap, with marked clipping of oversized individual pastes and attachment notes. JSON escaping, array delimiters and separators are charged. Initiating and newest turns survive; omissions are explicitly noted.

## Acceptance and review

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Unforgeable replay delimiters | Shared OpenCode builder and Python renderer generate fresh 128-bit nonces; synthetic pasted old headings/end markers remain unchanged inside one trusted end boundary |
| Rendered budget, including image-only and zero | Regression cases exercise 500 image-only entries, long notes, excerpt markers, saved-file pointer overhead and budgets 0/1000/2000/4000/64000; rendered text never exceeds the configured budget |
| Bounded V2 store | Production adapter tests exercise oversized pastes, escaped control characters, oversized attachment metadata, first-plus-newest retention and 1500 prompt entries |
| Hook and compaction compatibility | Python compile passes; all 35 scoped Node tests pass |

Independent final static review found no remaining patch-introduced defects for adapter-generated entries. First-round findings (JSON expansion, first-turn metadata, array accounting and missing single-turn elision) are repaired and covered. Review patch SHA-256: `accae8ded9486dc848b904d0abaf1d873fef52331fdb9848a90e21d8a98348c8`. The review-bundle helper was unavailable because this runner lacks the `file` utility; final-file independent review and direct diff inspection were used instead.

Final repaired patch SHA-256: `b0474523ebe80204cfcbdacba05ec9eb60125916526e5f78428d126fa7c4e7e3`. The sole post-review code change combines equivalent disabled/zero guards; direct diff and focused regression verification cover it.

Changelog

Sourced from anomalyco/opencode/github's changelog.

Changelog

Release notes for OpenCode V2, newest first.

v2.1.0 — 2026-10-20

Highlights

  • Persistent Terminals on Windows: Windows users now get persistent PTYs through the same terminal workflow available on macOS and Linux. (#56245)
  • Todo Lists in the TUI: Enable { "experimental": { "todo": true } } to give models the todowrite tool and display their task list in the session and sidebar. (#56947)
  • Reliable Long-Running TUI Commands: Plugin commands, shell calls, and other TUI requests can now run beyond Bun’s five-minute fetch deadline without losing their connection. (#55149)

Breaking changes

Version 2.1 makes intentional changes to public SDK, HTTP message/event, and plugin contracts so provider replay data and compaction use consistent names and shapes. Integrations must adopt the new fields. Existing stored sessions, credentials, and older session imports remain readable through compatibility decoders; no database migration is required. (#57260)

Provider replay data is now native

Provider-owned replay data previously used different names on different surfaces. Read and write native instead; a tool's execution state and UI metadata are separate and are not renamed.

Surface Before After
Text and reasoning parts state native
Assistant and compaction messages providerState native
Text/reasoning lifecycle events and session.tool.called state native
session.step.ended, session.step.failed, and session.compaction.ended providerState native
session.tool.success and session.tool.failed resultState native
Exported replay-data schema SessionMessage.ProviderState SessionMessage.Native
Plugin compaction hook result SessionCompactionResult.providerState SessionCompactionResult.native

Tool call and result data share tool.native

Tool parts no longer have separate providerState and providerResultState fields:

 tool
-  providerState?
-  providerResultState?
+  native?
   state

Success and failure events shallow-merge their native into the call's existing native. Missing result data preserves call data; result values win on duplicate keys. Provider/protocol implementations must use distinct keys when call and result values differ. There is no state.native, resultNative, or nested { call, result } envelope.

Replay passes the merged blob to the protocol, which reads the fields it needs. Tool calls receive it only for the same provider and model. Provider-run results receive it for the same provider, including after a model switch. Local results receive it only for the same provider and model when the step did not fail. Legacy stored or imported providerResultState is merged into tool.native when read. Execution status and readable output remain in tool.state.

Key credential setup answers move to metadata

Credential.Key.configuration is removed. Public credential writes must put setup-form answers in the existing metadata field:

title: GH#35170: fix OpenCode V2 headless workers denied shell/read/edit/skill

title: GH#35222: maintain and archive isolated OpenCode databases
body:
## Summary

Resolves #35222

- Add fixed-depth, NUL-delimited isolated database inventory shared by reporting and scheduled cleanup. Ignore discovered symlinks and avoid processing the selected database twice.
- Run the daily archive through `archive-all`, preserving the existing age/count policy and creating an archive beside each active database. Continue across protected live-holder skips.
- Run scheduled `auto` maintenance per database with independent isolated throttle/state records. Inspect the selected DB and existing WAL/SHM files; fail closed on lsof diagnostics rather than blocking idle projects because another project has an active TUI.
- Report active, WAL and archive sizes for all discovered project databases, even when the default database is absent.
- Add optional `--archive-event-retention-days N` / `OPENCODE_ARCHIVE_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS`. Default 0 disables expiry. Only archived event rows belonging to sessions inactive N days are removed; session/message/part transcripts remain. Freed pages are reused, not archive-VACUUMed. Document per-DB budgets and configuration in helper help.
- Make the no-candidate dry run non-mutating and accept explicit `--apply` while preserving legacy apply-by-default behavior.

## Files and reference pattern

Changed the three existing OpenCode DB helpers, added `opencode-db-inventory-lib.sh`, and extended the two existing SQLite fixture suites under `.agents/scripts/tests/`. Existing archive holder/WAL/schema checks and maintenance capacity/VACUUM guards remain the reference pattern.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk**: critical (opt-in deletion of archived event payloads)
- **Level**: runtime-verified using synthetic SQLite databases only; no operator DB was modified
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-maintenance.sh`: **35 passed, 0 failed**
- `env PRIVACY_REPOS_CONFIG=/dev/null PRIVACY_CACHE_FILE=/dev/null PRIVACY_ENTITY_CONFIG=/dev/null bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-opencode-db-archive.sh`: **39 passed, 0 failed**
- ShellCheck on all six changed shell files: clean; Bash syntax and `git diff --check`: clean
- Repository pre-push `bun run typecheck`: passed after the documented frozen-lockfile, ignore-scripts dependency setup
- Independent safety review identified an lsof exit-1 diagnostic ambiguity; repaired and covered by a protected-skip regression

### Pre-existing failure evidence

The archive suite without the three privacy configuration overrides reports 37 passed / 2 failed, both HOME-unset cases failing at unchanged `privacy-guard-helper.sh:38` with HOME unbound. `git blame` attributes lines 38-39 to pre-existing commit `a71863bfa7`; line 43 likewise expands HOME. Setting only those three existing configuration variables allows all 39 assertions to pass. No unrelated privacy-helper code is changed.

## Decisions

Expiry is opt-in to preserve saved histories by default. Package-internal names such as `node_modules/pkg/build` are never selected, so no dependency tree is partly removed.
  - A candidate must contain no tracked or unignored files, and must sit beside tracked sources. For example, `node_modules` inside an untracked packaged `.app` is kept.
  - Idleness uses file mtimes outside the candidates, plus the newest HEAD reflog entry's timestamp and HEAD's mtime. Directory mtimes, Finder `.DS_Store` writes and reflog-file rewrites by maintenance are ignored.

title: fix(worktrees): unify creation and rootless lifetime evidence (GH#35288)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #35288.

- Centralize host worktree creation and ownership registration in `shared-worktree-create.sh`, including CLI/profile, Pulse, release/recovery, planning, branch-cleanup, workflow-sync, plugin and archive-restore producers.
- Add rootless owner-cgroup observations and a bounded user-systemd runner. Only a recorded, closed invocation with the required descendant-completion contract can supply managed removal proof; PID disappearance is insufficient.
- Fence old completion receipts **before** Git recreates a path. A matching creation nonce is consumed atomically with registration; old generations are retained in history. Failed registration retains the fence, including when filesystem inode numbers are reused.
- Invalidate admission evidence for both paths when a legacy SQL writer moves an ownership row. Preserve managed temporary worktrees when completion evidence is unavailable rather than hiding cleanup failures or downgrading their backend.
- Preserve macOS synchronous legacy behavior without fabricating systemd receipts. No sudo, CI configuration changes or release publication are involved.

## Implementation and review focus

The shared entry point is `.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-create.sh`. Ownership transactions live in `shared-worktree-registry-owner.py`; observation, admission and receipt validation live in `worktree_lifetime_owner.py`, `worktree-managed-lifetime.py` and `worktree_lifetime_proof.py`. `worktree-managed-run.py` owns only its uniquely named user service. Producer-specific branch/ref policies remain with their existing callers.

The existing managed-lifetime/guard contract is the reference pattern. Backend differences and deferred retirement are documented in `.agents/reference/platform-support.md`. Independent static review identified inode-reuse and path-move admission cases; both were repaired and regression-covered before this PR.

The CI complexity findings were addressed by simplifying ownership dispatch and capability/startup checks, separating bounded output transport into `worktree_managed_io.py`, and separating runner contract tests from owner-lifetime tests. No CI settings, ratchet thresholds or override labels were changed.

## Verification

- Native Linux owner lifecycle and runner contracts: **18 owner tests + 6 runner tests passed**, including creation → work → descendant completion → Git-only capture → guarded removal → restore → failed recreation → successful same-path recreation. Restoration compares HEAD, index, staged changes and unstaged tracked changes; untracked files are intentionally not included.
- Managed lifetime: **21 tests passed**, including the native user-systemd descendant/guard case.
- Workflow sync: **65 assertions passed**. Fixtures now model public-repository visibility, durable PR identity/origin labels, and both required mirror workflows; production privacy and mirror guards remain enabled.
- Release-helper suite passed with mocked Git/publication and isolated process fixtures. Native creation/registration is exercised separately by the owner lifecycle suite.
- Earlier producer checks passed for aggregate/dead-preparing recovery, scratch creation/reaping, WordPress creation, fallback/restore paths, and local/remote branch cleanup and dirty-PR handling in the tested managed/legacy configurations.
- `linters-local.sh --base-ref origin/main --strict --no-cache` passed changed-file gates; ShellCheck, secretlint, Bash 3.2 compatibility, portability and complexity regression gates passed. Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed. Markdownlint is not installed locally and remains delegated to CI.

## Limitations and safety

Native macOS execution is unavailable; Darwin/backend selection is tested through simulation and shell portability checks, not claimed as a native Mac result. Registration alone does not start supervision: generic producers outside a managed run retain unavailable completion evidence and must not be automatically removed on that basis. Existing legacy trees are not retroactively given managed completion receipts.

body:
## Summary

Resolves #35499

- Keep the full-loop plugin test gate enabled on saturated worker hosts: above a one-minute load average of 4 per available CPU, run its test files serially.
- Allow the plugin test script to honor `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_TEST_CONCURRENCY`; unset means the existing Node default, preserving direct npm and CI behavior.
- Scope automatic adaptation to the plugin test phase, with no changes to test budgets, assertions, or CI workflows. A failed load probe conservatively selects serial execution.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`: configure concurrency inside the existing scoped command subshell, after runtime selection.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/package.json`: optional concurrency flag before the test file glob.
- The issue's canonical Files Scope records the validator module move from its parent helper.

## Verification

Node v24.21.0 / npm 11.19.0; root engine requires Node >=20. Locked root and plugin dependencies installed without lifecycle scripts.

- PASS: load selection probes for 0/16, exactly 64/16 (unchanged), 64.1/16 (serial), and a failed load probe (serial fallback).
- PASS: all 18 bounded-operation tests in both full-suite executions, including timeout, containment and restoration assertions.
- PASS: production `_run_scoped_node_checks` selected serial npm execution with process-local simulated load 80/16. Its check-only snapshot guard preserved the clean worktree, and it correctly reported real suite failures rather than swallowing them.
- PASS: push-time `bun run typecheck`, shell syntax checks, diff whitespace checks, and pre-commit ratchets.
- `npm run test`: 1170 passed, 23 failed, 1 skipped (62.2s). Serial production gate: 1171 passed, 22 failed, 1 skipped (132.2s). These runs are NOT reported as green.

Unrelated runner failures: unchanged fixtures in `test-git-safety-gate.mjs:40`, `test-hook-status-tool.mjs`, `test-pre-edit-tool-workdir.mjs`, `test-signature-footer-gate.mjs`, and `test-source-access-approval.mjs` hard-code `/usr/bin/git` or `/usr/bin/ssh-keygen`, absent on this NixOS host (tools exist on the host PATH). `test-source-access-approval.mjs:131` also expects `/usr/bin/python3` instead of the host-selected Python. The default-concurrency run additionally failed `test-mcp-activation.mjs:690` on a missing fixture artifact; that test passed serially. No plugin runtime or test files changed in this PR. These out-of-scope failures were not repaired or suppressed.

ShellCheck is unavailable locally: the PATH wrapper reports `cannot find real shellcheck binary`. `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` `cross-platform-shellcheck` covers the shell module. `bash -n`, `git diff --check`, and pre-commit ratchets passed.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: low. Runtime-verified load selection and production scoped validator invocation; relevant bounded-operation tests pass. Full-suite local failures and unavailable static lint are explicitly disclosed above for CI verification.

## Acceptance self-review

- High load: the production gate runs the entire plugin suite serially; reported failures are therefore already observed serially. Verified with injected load readings, not a claim of physically saturating the host.
- Unloaded host: the npm command expands to the existing `node --test tests/*.mjs` arguments, and only one short Node load probe is added in full-loop. No measured baseline comparison is claimed.
- No test budgets or assertions changed. CI workflow and its direct Node test invocation are unchanged.

## Decisions

Use concurrency 1 rather than 2 above the threshold so any reported test failure already reproduces without competing test files. Unloaded hosts retain the same suite concurrency and incur only one short Node load probe during the local plugin validator.

title: GH#35517: feat(opencode-db): idle-gated archive of DBs held by idle OpenCode sessions
body:
## Summary

OpenCode open 24/7 with workers kept the session DBs permanently held, so the nightly archive always deferred and the DB kept growing. New plugin heartbeat (db-activity-heartbeat.mjs, wired into index.mjs) writes per-process busy-session count, last-activity time and open session IDs to ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/state/opencode-activity/<pid>-<instance>.json. New opencode-db-idle-gate-lib.sh lets opencode-db-archive.sh proceed on a held DB only when every holder is an opencode process whose heartbeats (written after that process started, defeating PID reuse) show zero busy sessions for 15 min, and keyboard/mouse is idle 30 min where measurable (ioreg / xprintidle). Held mode archives 10 sessions per transaction, re-checks the gate before every batch (pausing with committed work kept), excludes sessions the holders have open plus their children, and skips VACUUM while held. The scheduler now runs hourly 00:00-07:00 (launchd plist builder extracted to _opencode_db_archive_plist) and opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh skips once a full pass completed today (OPENCODE_DB_ARCHIVE_FORCE=1 overrides). title: t18767: fix(pulse): make worker admission RAM-only (GH#35537)
body:
## Summary

Owner directive (2026-10-23): Macs and servers schedule their own CPU and can run every core at 100% for sustained periods. **RAM is the only host resource that may limit worker admission.** This PR removes every CPU-based admission throttle, records the directive as durable policy, and adds a CI guard so it cannot drift back.

Resolves #35537

## Evidence

- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` on a 16-core / 128 GB Mac: `admission=closed` x2 and `admission=idle_headroom` x56, e.g. `load=70.62/16 cpu_gate=open_idle cpu_idle_pct=55 idle_slots=8 active_workers=0` — the CPU gate held the host at 8 new workers with 55% CPU idle and ~33-38 GB reclaimable RAM.
- The automatic cap was `50% of logical cores` (GH#32663) = 8 on this host, regardless of RAM.
- Measured worker process trees: 0.7-1.6 GB each, versus the old `RAM_PER_WORKER_MB=512` estimate.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`: delete `_pulse_cpu_pressure`, load/core/idle probes and `_pulse_cap_idle_headroom`. Add `_pulse_ram_available_mb`, `_pulse_ram_worker_growth_mb` (reserves RAM young workers have not claimed yet, from one `ps` snapshot) and `_pulse_ram_admission`. The refill cap now clamps to `active + RAM slots`; the minimum-worker floor can never exceed RAM headroom.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh`: `calculate_max_workers` = running workers + RAM slots, then explicit/auto cap and shared-host division. Logs `admission_policy=ram_only`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh`: automatic cap = `(total RAM - reserve) / RAM_PER_WORKER_MB`, clamped 2-64 (no core count). `RAM_PER_WORKER_MB` default 512 -> 1536.
- Config: `orchestration.max_load_per_core` and `cpu_idle_admit_percent` marked deprecated and ignored (schema, defaults, `config-helper.sh` env map).
- `.agents/reference/configuration.md`: new **Worker resource policy** section — the directive, the formula, what is *not* an admission throttle (`DISPATCH_MAX_PARALLEL`, boot ramp, watchdog CPU-idle stall detection, validator serial plugin tests), and how to correct future regressions.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-ram-admission.sh` (replaces `test-pulse-cpu-admission.sh`): static guard fails if admission scripts read load average, CPU idle or core counts; dynamic guard runs the production admission path with a saturated-CPU stub (load 999, 0% idle) and fails if any CPU probe is called. Added to the `Worker Count and Capacity Tests` CI step.

## Out of scope

Launch-ceremony concurrency (`DISPATCH_MAX_PARALLEL`), the boot/cooldown dispatch ramp, worker-watchdog CPU-idle stall detection, and the full-loop validator's serial plugin-test mode (test determinism, GH#35499). None of these gate admission.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-ram-admission.sh` — 42 PASS, including a clean-`HOME` CI simulation.
- `test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh` 31/31, `test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh` 27/27, `test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh` 54/54, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count.sh` 57/57, `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` 69/69, `test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`, `test-maintenance-selector-contract.sh` all pass.
- `shellcheck -x` clean on all changed scripts; schema JSON parses; actionlint clean.
- Static guard against `origin/main`: 23 CPU-telemetry matches in `pulse-capacity.sh`, 3 in `pulse-wrapper-config.sh` (guard would have failed the old code).
- Live read-only probe on this host: `slots=14 available_mb=31444 growth_mb=3387 workers_seen=4` -> target 18 (previously capped at 8 by core count and idle headroom).

title: chore(deps): bump filelock from 3.29.4 to 4.2.1 in the pip group across 1 directory
body:
Bumps the pip group with 1 update in the / directory: [filelock](https://github.com/tox-dev/py-filelock). Updates `filelock` from 3.29.4 to 4.2.1
Release notes

Sourced from filelock's releases.

4.2.1

  • On a singleton wrapper, close> and close> end only the holds that tasks acquired through that wrapper. A reader that arrives during close() gets the closed error instead of joining the ending hold. After synchronous code closes or force-releases the shared lock, the wrappers refuse to admit readers into the ended hold, and close() on such a wrapper returns. Closing one wrapper no longer ends a task's nested hold taken through another wrapper on the same path. #832
  • ReadWriteLock locks again after a release() that an exception from a signal handler interrupted. The async read-write wrappers stop admitting readers into such a level. The async read-write locks forget a hold whose backend release failed after the backend let go, and they free the memory of each acquire that times out or is canceled. AsyncFileLock returns from release() after a few hundred acquires gave up behind a waiting one. An exception from a signal handler delivered while an AsyncFileLock call joins its queue no longer blocks every later call on that lock. #833
  • Fix ReadWriteLock acting on -journal, -wal or -shm files another process puts beside its database: a write could land in another file, a reader could get in beside a writer, and an acquire could fail. SQLite now opens the database by name only in a directory no other account can write, and through a private hard link elsewhere. On Windows the directory's access control list decides. Where hard links are unavailable, keep the database in a directory other accounts cannot write, such as one under %LOCALAPPDATA%. The lock removes link directories through a checked descriptor rather than by name, reads a link directory's name only when the locking account owns it, and leaves alone a directory with other content renamed onto a link directory's name. A database whose schema takes more than a few kilobytes to load raises ValueError instead of running past the acquire timeout. #834
  • Fix five bugs in opening the lock file. UnixFileLock no longer truncates a file it did not create, such as one renamed to the lock path, and no longer applies mode to it. An on_acquired hook that writes holder metadata now truncates the file itself. A lease (Linux) or an oplock (Windows) on the lock file or a soft lock's marker no longer holds acquire() past its timeout or blocking=False, and an oplock no longer holds release(); ReadWriteLock on Windows waits for its timeout and raises Timeout. On Windows, a mode without group and other bits, such as 0o600, now creates the lock file with an owner-only permission list; the ReadWriteLock database gets the same. The soft locks' writability check no longer follows a symlink swapped in at the lock path. On a filesystem without flock, a contender from another account now waits on a marker it cannot write instead of raising PermissionError. #835
  • Fix SoftFileLock, MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease removing a live holder's marker in three cases: the holder and the contender run in Linux time namespaces with different boottime offsets; only one of them can read the boot id; a process other than the owner rewrote the marker. Soft markers no longer carry group or other write bits. A process name containing a carriage return or another line separator no longer makes the stale check raise ValueError. When /proc/self/ns/time exists but cannot be read, the stale check no longer compares start times and keeps the marker. #836
  • The async read-write locks record their hold under a task owner, so synchronous code on the executor thread that took the hold can no longer re-enter or release it. AsyncSoftReadWriteLock gives back one level on release, so synchronous readers of a shared singleton keep theirs. SoftReadWriteLock tracks read levels per thread: release() from a thread that holds none raises RuntimeError. After its heartbeat recorded a lost hold, it refuses new acquires until that hold is released. #838
  • StrictSoftFileLock creates <path>.filelock and its claims directory with the lock's mode and sets the sticky bit (a directory flag that lets only a file's owner remove it) on both. On the next acquisition it narrows a directory it owns that an earlier release created wider; it leaves a directory of another account as it is, so remove such leftovers by hand. It reaches claims through a descriptor opened without following symlinks; on Windows it holds both directories open and refuses a junction (a directory that points at another directory). Under a sticky parent such as /tmp it refuses a coordination directory of another account, as SoftReadWriteLock does for <path>.rw. One read grace now covers a whole claim scan, a failed claim cleanup no longer leaves the sentinel descriptor open, and a non-regular node at a sentinel private-record name raises SoftFileLockProtocolError. On Windows, contenders read claims without blocking their owner's unlink. #839

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from filelock's changelog.

4.2.3 (2026-10-19)

  • Creating a lock on a Python 3.15 interpreter without types.LazyImportType no longer triggers AttributeError at exit. :pr:860
  • Handle EFTYPE when a no-follow open refuses a symlink in a soft reader/writer lock's protocol tree, so heartbeat reports lost ownership rather than a transient refresh error.

4.2.2 (2026-10-18)

  • Fix a lock on a relative path that stayed held after a later with lock: ended, when an earlier acquire() had failed because the working directory no longer exists. That call still raises :class:FileNotFoundError, and it now leaves the lock's hold count unchanged. :pr:856

Bumps the npm_and_yarn group with 1 update in the /.agents directory: [fast-uri](https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri). Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.8 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

title: GH#35529: surface cancellation receipts for interrupted Task parts and classify native UI actions
body:
## Summary

When the operator interrupts a running Task, OpenCode marks the in-flight Task part status:error / 'Tool execution aborted' / metadata.interrupted and never produces a Task result, so tool.execute.after (the only place the t18148 cancellation receipt was attached) never ran and the parent saw only the bare error. Native desktop calls were also missing from every receipt because the classifier keyed on write verbs. Changes: (1) subagent-side-effect-classifier.mjs classifies macos-automator_execute_script, macos-automator_accessibility_query command=perform and bash osascript as desktop.native_ui; (2) subagent-cancellation-ledger.mjs keeps interrupted child calls in flight so they report outcome unknown, not failed; (3) subagent-cancellation-receipt.mjs detects the interrupted Task part event, finalizes the existing bounded receipt once (lifecycle terminal evidence first, one abort request only if termination is still unconfirmed), persists it through recordReceipt, and exposes injectReceipts; (4) index.mjs messages transform appends the receipt plus a one-line read-only recovery pointer (child session ID, session-introspect-helper.sh / opencode export) to that interrupted Task result in each outgoing request, leaving stored history unchanged; (5) agent-routing.md adds the recovery clause.



## Files Changed

body:
## Summary

Resolves #35536 when acceptance verification is complete and this PR is merged.

Implement `aidevops tabby sessions new|restore|list|doctor` from the merged t18766 specification (planning PR #35535), without changing profile reconciliation or deploying anything.

This is an **interactive, manual implementation**. Keep the issue's `no-auto-dispatch` label. No autonomous implementation worker was launched.

## Current acceptance audit (self-review)

Head: `d00385507247f6a9341b06ce5d06dbcf9c1c7e5f`. Runtime code is unchanged from `4d0c8499f`; the final commit adds the required README quick-start link and passes scoped Markdown/secret/whitespace gates plus normal commit/push hooks.

Rebuilt closeout bundle: schema `aidevops.review-evidence/v1`, SHA-256 `cb208c80e718a12db08abe41ccc65e366b099a282f6606b432b3be087714fe0b`, base `7fede4449d779689fa02e85fef0def6af1d96884`, head as above, prompt-injection scan clean. Independent production-code findings and focused proof apply to unchanged code; the final README addition received direct diff inspection. This bundle is defect-review evidence, not a blind independent acceptance verdict.

The authoritative source is the specification merged by planning PR #35535, section **Acceptance criteria** (source lines 180-194). Earlier chronological notes incorrectly treated a successful same-device Mac concurrent-SSH run as a separate mandatory platform gate. The specification requires tested concurrent deduplication, plus real Linux/macOS attachment, persistence and repeat-restore smoke evidence; it does not require every live scenario on every OS. This correction does not claim that the inconclusive Mac concurrency attempt passed or that its SSH failure was diagnosed. No SSH repair, administrator action, or further parallel probe is required merely to satisfy an invented gate.

| Criterion | Status | Evidence and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing profile behavior | satisfied | Profile implementation/tests unchanged; 23 shell regressions pass. Python regressions retain the same three reproduced baseline NixOS failures, recorded below, not falsely reported green. |
| Atomic numbering, no automatic OpenCode | satisfied | Creation/collision/uncertainty coverage; four parallel production allocations against an isolated real tmux server; live detached creation on both laptops. |
| Enabled-host restore and accurate aggregation | satisfied | Config-order/disabled-host tests, continued processing after failure, and preserved requested counts after a partial host failure. |
| Repeated/concurrent restore and pending UI limits | satisfied | Linux live overlap yielded one tab/confirmation; native isolated concurrency passed on both OSes; both live sequential GUI checks passed. Expired production backend refused attachment without changing the reservation; the original brief GUI message was not observed. Empty/stale confirmation tabs are explicitly outside attachment-idempotency guarantees. |
| Supported legacy and independent laptops | satisfied | Allowlisted direct-SSH parser/rename-ambiguity tests and documented exclusions; physical Linux/Mac shared-shell marker plus connected observations on both laptops passed. |
| Recovery and outdated identifiers | satisfied | Native lease/expiry/orphan/reassignment tests, live disconnect/persistence/reopen evidence on both laptops, live expired-backend refusal, and corrupt unlocked-state refusal. |
| Renames and equivalent aliases | satisfied | Stable-key/alias/legacy-ambiguity tests, isolated real tmux rename check, documented endpointId grouping and prefix boundaries. Final interactive attachment now rechecks identity/prefix inside the same tmux server. |
| Empty/missing/invalid/broken dependencies | satisfied | Distinct inventory/config/identity/tmux/CLI errors, dry-run/list/doctor side-effect checks, and live empty-inventory doctors. |
| Natural order and service exclusion | satisfied | Numeric/named ordering and unrelated-prefix/delimiter tests; no tab-closing/reordering code. |
| Safe paths and argv | satisfied | Isolated paths with spaces/metacharacters, validated aliases/names, nested POSIX quoting assertions; actual Mac local Tabby argv probe passed. |
| Privacy and SSH safeguards | satisfied | Generic committed examples, sanitized errors, current-account process scope, secret checks, fixed SSH argv; no real inventory/authentication logs published and no SSH safeguards changed. |
| Existing titles and opt-in clipboard | satisfied | Existing title owner unchanged, transparent byte-relay coverage, remote synthetic full-title delivery on both platforms, reviewed manual title snippet and explicit clipboard-write trust boundary. No live OpenCode status/window-title or enabled clipboard smoke claim. |
| Real Linux/macOS platform smoke | satisfied | Each laptop demonstrated attached state, controlled same-shell persistence after tab closure, repeat-restore CLI/GUI suppression and full-title delivery; versions and revision boundaries are recorded below. Latest guard has separate real Linux tmux/PTY evidence, not a relabeled Mac GUI rerun. |

This table is the implementing session's structured acceptance self-review, not an independent acceptance approval. Separate bounded independent code reviews covered the production modules; the verified session-identity race was repaired and its changed code reviewed again. The legacy endpoint-override suggestion was rejected because those direct-SSH forms are explicitly outside the supported migration grammar.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk: high; evidence: runtime-verified with explicit coverage limits.** Earlier Linux/macOS GUI checks are pinned below, not relabeled as latest-head GUI runs.
- Final guard verification used tmux **3.6a**, an owned isolated socket, empty config, and a real local PTY client. Stale creation time, stale server PID, rename outside the prefix, and session-ID reuse after restarting only the owned server all refused attachment with zero clients. A matching identity attached; terminating only the owned local client preserved the remote session. Only SSH transport/socket selection was substituted; no real SSH endpoint or ongoing work was used. An empty newly created lock remains usable; busy locks retain conservative `pending` behavior while their metadata may be mid-write. Existing state is preserved, not deleted or rewritten to force recovery.
- The focused regression failed in all four malformed-metadata cases before the production fix, then passed. The complete existing session runner now reports **36 tests passed** on the agent's Linux host. Its isolated filesystem locks are real; SSH and Tabby transports remain mocked. No live reservations, remote sessions or tabs were used for the new regression.
- **23 existing shell profile regressions passed** using the existing isolated dependency environment. Python compilation, `git diff --check`, exact-head affected-scope linters against 622b2b373, and scoped Qlty structural checks passed. Normal commit/push hooks passed, including `bun run typecheck`; no hook bypass was used.
- A bounded code-only advisory review found no concrete issue in the new guard and regression. This is not a full independent implementation approval or platform/runtime smoke evidence. Earlier broad advisory input was incomplete; its raw-mode concern was checked against versioned OpenSSH 10.5p1 and 8.6p1 source, where PTY-backed raw mode operates on stdin rather than requiring terminal stdout. No speculative PTY rewrite or new test infrastructure was added.
- **Operator-confirmed Mac rerun passed on 6f3c00840:** the isolated checkout fast-forwarded from eace4aa2e to 6f3c00840, and the unchanged runner reported **36 tests in 0.169 seconds, OK**. This verifies the new corrupt-state guard and its regression on macOS using isolated filesystem fixtures and mocked SSH/Tabby transports; it is not live concurrent-SSH or same-session two-laptop acceptance.
- Both laptops' live smoke results above predate this guard and are not relabeled as live tests of this revision. Exact-head repository revalidation found all six required checks successful and no pending or unsuccessful reported check/status contexts. The bounded ten-minute check watcher reached its time limit; a subsequent exact-head Framework Validation run query confirmed terminal success, followed by a fresh complete PR-check observation. This PR remains draft. Nothing was merged, released or deployed; no new live SSH probes or autonomous implementation worker were launched in this follow-up.

### Renewed same-session two-laptop check: passed

- The operator confirmed that a common account/tmux target is available through existing aliases on both laptops. A separate private Mac inventory and independent local state path were prepared with a fresh random disposable prefix, without overwriting existing inventories or changing SSH settings. The read-only doctor passed with Tabby 1.0.234, Python 3.14 and **zero matching sessions**; state was not initialized before launch.
- One Mac `new pair` reported **created=1 requested=1 failed=0**. A subsequent `list pair` reported **connected=1 failed=0**. This verifies detached creation and a managed Mac attachment for the new fixture; requested alone was not treated as authentication proof.
- A guarded command checked the current tmux pane's exact disposable session name before exporting a synthetic shell marker. The operator reported **shared_marker=pair-still-here-35536** from the Mac fixture. This established the Mac shell baseline before Linux attached; common-target availability alone was not treated as proof of namespace equivalence.
- Through a separate private Linux inventory using that exact disposable prefix and independent local state, the operator's initial `list pair` found the Mac-created fixture as **missing=1 connected=0 failed=0 created=0**. Linux was instructed to restore this existing fixture, never create another session or export/reset the marker there.
- The operator then reported the original **shared_marker=pair-still-here-35536** from the Linux fixture, followed by both Linux and Mac `list pair` outputs identifying that same disposable session with **connected=1 missing=0 failed=0**. Shared-shell continuity and managed attachment observations from both physical laptops therefore pass. The Linux restore command's own stdout and separate GUI tab counts were not supplied and are not invented. This closes the same-session two-laptop evidence gap; it does not establish same-device Mac concurrent-restore behavior or resolve the earlier handshake/transport failure. No overlapping SSH diagnostic probes were added by this check.
- The operator explicitly confirmed that the Mac shared-session target is the **same server and account** as the earlier failing Mac concurrency target. The prior SSH handshake/transport blocker therefore remains relevant; a different target is not used to claim it resolved. Parallel probes remain paused. Any further server-side check is limited to nonprivileged, read-only admission-policy inspection through the already-open disposable session, with no authentication logs, private connection details, configuration changes or automatic privilege escalation.
- A guarded, nonprivileged `sshd -T` default-configuration check through that existing disposable shell reported **default_sshd_policy=unavailable**. No policy values were obtained. This does not establish that permissions, admission limits, or any particular configuration caused the failure. No `sudo`, authentication-log collection, configuration changes, package installation or further parallel SSH attempts followed. Mac concurrent-restore acceptance is **externally blocked for this session**, owned by the operator/their SSH administrator for private diagnosis; the cause remains unknown. Resume that acceptance path only after the private SSH issue is understood or resolved sufficiently for a bounded retest, preserving existing authentication and host-verification safeguards.
- Repository revalidation at unchanged head **6f3c00840f49e261be4ca0867a844858043dce65** found a clean source worktree and **all six required checks successful**. Issue #35536 remains open with `no-auto-dispatch`; the PR remains open and draft. Successful checks and the shared-session pass do not waive the unresolved Mac concurrent-restore acceptance criterion. Nothing was merged, released or deployed.

## Known limitations and historical observations

1. Mac live same-device concurrent restore remains inconclusive: overlapping SSH probes yielded one handshake/transport failure with no specific cause established. Sequential production requests and the shared-session two-laptop test passed. Parallel probes are paused. Historical statements above that this was a mandatory separate platform acceptance blocker are superseded by the specification-based audit at the top; no pass or root cause is invented. The first Linux fixture's earlier disappearance also remains unexplained, separate from subsequent controlled persistence passes. The original brief GUI expiry message was not observed; separate production-backend refusal was verified. Disposable tests were authorized and operator-run on the laptops; no ongoing user work or authentication logs were collected.
2. Existing Python profile-regression portability failures above remain visible; they are not reported as passing and were not hidden by modifying unrelated tests.
3. The 120-second reservation protects managed attachments, not empty/stale confirmation tabs. An expired confirmation refuses attachment; a live authentication wrapper holds its lease until exit.
4. Legacy support is explicitly bounded. Unknown renamed targets conservatively skip that endpoint; unmanaged launches racing after the check cannot be serialized. Different textual DNS aliases require an explicit shared non-sensitive `endpointId`.
5. Inventory/creation probes require privately prepared noninteractive OpenSSH authentication. Five-second default pacing is not authentication-completion evidence. Title/clipboard setup remains manual and opt-in; no competing title writer or remote configuration mutation is introduced.

Continue the ready-PR review/check gates. Merge only if repository policy and permissions permit. Keep `no-auto-dispatch`; do not publish a release or deploy this PR.

title: GH#35407: refactor: extract change-plan value and term-usage helpers
body:
## Summary

Resolves #35407. For #35365 (parent stays open).

The Qlty `file-complexity` score for `.agents/scripts/wp-change-plan.php` goes down because two separate jobs now live in their own files. Behaviour does not change.

- `.agents/scripts/wp-change-plan-values.php` — new `WPCP_Values` class holding the pure helpers the planner uses to compare and print values: `label`, `same`, `normalize`, `show`, `single`, `is_string_list`, `sorted`. Their bodies are the same as before. They are now public static, and their callers use `WPCP_Values::` instead of `self::`.
- `.agents/scripts/wp-change-plan-term-usage.php` — new `WPCP_Term_Usage` class holding the read-only scan that runs before a term is deleted. It checks posts, child terms, nav menu items and ACF/SCF values (`acf_term_references`, `acf_table_references`, `acf_reference_value`, `collect_taxonomy_field_keys`, `value_has_term`, `id_list`). The old `term_usage()` is now `WPCP_Term_Usage::describe()`, and only `evaluate_delete()` calls it.
- `.agents/scripts/wp-change-plan.php` loads both files with `require_once __DIR__ . '/…'`. WP-CLI `eval-file` rewrites `__DIR__` to the script's real directory, and the runs below confirm it. Public signatures, permission checks, backup-before-write, write order, read-back, restore and CLI output are unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/wp-helper-change-plan.sh`: a new `WPCP_PHP_FILES` list and a `_wpcp_upload_scripts` function upload all three PHP files into the private `mktemp -d` directory on SSH sites. Before this change only `wp-change-plan.php` was uploaded. LocalWP still runs the scripts in place from `SCRIPT_DIR`.
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-change-plan.md` now notes that the three files must stay together.

Five files changed, which is the scope limit.

## Qlty (same version, same mode)

`qlty 0.657.0`, `qlty smells --all --sarif --no-snippets --quiet`, run on `origin/main` 70b73a8db0 and on this branch:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `qlty:file-complexity` on `wp-change-plan.php` | 519 | 456 |
| findings in the whole repository | 36 | 36 |
| findings in the new files | — | 0 |

Function cognitive complexity in the new files is at most 11 (`collect_taxonomy_field_keys`). Each new file is well under the 50 file-complexity threshold, so the new-file gate should pass. CI pins Qlty 0.643.0. These numbers come from 0.657.0 and are not compared with 0.643.0 results.

**Remaining finding:** `wp-change-plan.php` is still above the threshold (456 > 50). Most of what remains is the evaluate, apply and restore logic, which shares the planner's instance state (`$backup`, `$taxonomies`, `$plan_path`). Splitting it would mean passing that state between objects and would go past the five-file limit. That work should be its own scoped task rather than part of this PR.

## Codacy (advisory, not a required check)

Codacy reports 104 new issues. 93 are Info-level PHPCS PEAR or Generic style rules, such as long array syntax, Yoda conditions and PEAR indentation, and they conflict with the WordPress coding style this file already follows. Of the 11 Warnings:

- 8 are `Squiz_Operators_ComparisonOperatorUsage` (`!` and implicit truthiness). They sit on lines that were moved unchanged, and the same constructs remain throughout `wp-change-plan.php`.
- 3 are PHPMD `StaticAccess` on the new `WPCP_Values::` and `WPCP_Term_Usage::` calls. The script already makes static calls such as `WP_CLI::line` throughout. Turning the helpers into objects just to satisfy this rule would add state and would not make the code easier to maintain.

These are not hand-applied because they would contradict the file's existing standard. Codacy also reports complexity on `wp-change-plan.php` going down by 41.

## Verification

- PHP 8.5.11 CLI: `php -l` passes on all three PHP files.
- `shellcheck` and `bash -n` pass on `wp-helper-change-plan.sh`. `git diff --check` is clean.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main` reports ALL LOCAL CHECKS PASSED.
- LocalWP fixture: Local "Plugin Testing" site, WordPress 7.1.3, PHP 8.5.3, WP-CLI bundled with Local, SCF active. I exported the database first. All test objects were throwaway (one draft post, three category terms) and were deleted afterwards. No live site was touched.
  - **Dry run, origin/main script against this branch.** Three plans: a post and term edit; deleting a term that is in use (post, child term and SCF taxonomy-field reference, with the SCF field registered for the run through `--require`); deleting an unused term. Output was identical and exit codes matched (0, 1, 0). The ACF reference is reported as `1 ACF field value(s): post <id> wpcp_qa_region`.
  - **Apply then restore, origin/main script against this branch, run directly with `wp eval-file`.** Both plans pass with exit 0 for apply and for restore, with read-back OK and every value restored. Once backup paths, the script path in the RESTORE hint, recreated term ids and caching-plugin noise are normalised, the output is identical.
  - **`wp-helper.sh --change-plan`, LocalWP transport.** Apply and restore both exit 0 for both plans.
  - **`wp-helper.sh --change-plan`, SSH transport.** `ssh` and `scp` were replaced by local stubs, and no real server was involved. The trace shows the three PHP files and the plan uploaded side by side, `wp eval-file` run from the uploaded directory, the backup downloaded, and the remote temp directory removed with the removal checked. Apply and restore both exit 0.
  - After every round the site state matched the starting snapshot, and no remote temp directories were left behind.
- No planner tests exist and none were added.

## Regression Evidence

The repository has no WordPress test harness. The planner only runs inside WP-CLI against a real database, and #35407 says new test infrastructure needs separate authority. Regression coverage for this PR is the differential run described under Verification. The origin/main script and this branch were run against the same LocalWP fixture for dry run, apply and restore, and their output matched once run-specific paths and ids were normalised. The SSH upload path was run end to end with local ssh/scp stubs, and every round returned the site to its starting state.

body:
## Summary

Two-part fix, as the issue specifies. (1) No publish-then-abort: _dlw_prelaunch_budget_available (moved to pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh beside _dlw_pre_runtime_failure so launch.sh stays under the 2000-line gate) gains a 'publication' mode that needs AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_PUBLICATION_RESERVE_SECONDS (default 75 = assign_and_label max of about 51 s plus live guard/spawn of about 25 s; 0 disables it; invalid values use the default) left before the deadline. It runs before the issue lock, before the final ownership fence and again just before _dlw_assign_and_label. A short reserve aborts through the existing exact-claim cleanup path with the new reason pre_runtime_failure:prelaunch_reserve_insufficient. An expired deadline keeps prelaunch_budget_exhausted. Lease TTL arithmetic, the no-slide deadline, orphan grace and claim consensus are unchanged. (2) precreate.* sub-stages: dispatch-stage-instrument.sh adds _ds_substage_start/_ds_substage_record/_ds_substage_run. These record only while the dispatcher exports AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_STAGE_ISSUE/_REPO, so interactive worktree creation writes nothing. worktree-helper-add.sh and shared-worktree-create.sh time capacity_check, create_worktree, stale/unmerged remote checks, sibling_status, scratch_add, base_fetch, registry_begin_create, git_worktree_add, registry_register, verify_generation, managed_enroll, helper_deps, exclusions and preview_routes. title: feat(worktrees): add explicit legacy maintenance workflow
body:
## Summary

Add explicit **user-space-only** `aidevops cleanup maintenance` for legacy worktrees without historical descendant-completion receipts. The earlier system-service design has been removed: no administrative access, privileged inspector, rescue target or session shutdown is needed or requested.

- Read-only, bounded `plan` batches (default 50, max 200), `check`, and explicitly confirmed `apply` through the existing archive-first cleaner, without `--force`.
- Version-2 plans bind the machine, user, repository/default tip, source identity, HEAD and original lifecycle record. Version-1 plans must be regenerated.
- Reuse the unprivileged procfs collector. Positive CWD matches always veto; unresolved or unusable visibility retains the source. Plan confirmation is not a lifetime receipt.
- Reuse Pulse retention predicates, including protective labels on closed PRs, enrichment/repair attribution and fail-closed malformed/truncated lookups.
- Preserve dirty work, ignored content, forensic markers, live owners, interrupted archives and unpublished history. Never rewrite historical lifecycle rows or fall through from failed maintenance proof to claim/seal or degraded recovery.

## Implementation and reference patterns

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-maintenance.py`: planner, user-bound confirmation, independent proof and archive-first application.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_maintenance_boundary.py`: user/boot context and candidate-local checks using `worktree_process_proc.collect` directly, without subprocess privilege elevation.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-process-policy.sh`: disables the optional privileged inspector whenever maintenance is requested; ordinary behavior remains unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-maintenance-policy.sh`: shared Pulse retention adapter.
- `.agents/scripts/audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`: proof at preparation and final native-removal boundaries, preserving historical records and existing CWD guards.
- `aidevops.sh`, `.agents/scripts/storage-cleanup-helper.sh`: CLI routing; maintenance is excluded from routine `all --apply`.
- `.agents/reference/worktree-legacy-maintenance.md`, `.agents/workflows/worktree-cleanup.md`: user-space contract and explicit retention limitations.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-maintenance.py`: existing unittest suite and archive fixture, real Git capture/removal/independent restore and unchanged SQLite-record assertions.

## Verification

title: GH#35723: operator-owned local-ai-providers override that survives aidevops update
body:
## Summary

Adds an operator-owned local-provider list at `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/aidevops/local-ai-providers.conf`. When the file exists it **replaces** the bundled `configs/local-ai-providers.conf` in both enforcement points. It lives outside the versioned runtime bundle, so `aidevops update` no longer reverts an operator's local provider IDs.

Resolves #35723

## Maintainer repairs applied (review comment on #35723)

1. **Reuse the stricter trust check.** `assertOperatorConfigStat` moved from `private-processing-policy.mjs` to `local-only-policy.mjs` and is exported. `private-processing-policy.mjs` imports it, so there is no import cycle. It requires a regular file that is not a symlink, mode exactly `0600`, size ≤ 64 KiB and current-user ownership.
2. **Write protection.** `assertClassificationMutation` and `assertShellRead` now protect the override path as well as `local-only-roots.json` (write/edit/apply_patch targets, relative targets and aliases, and shell/bounded-operation commands that name the path). The check runs in bound and unbound sessions, and whether or not the file exists.
3. **Headless endpoint gap documented.** The "Trust assumptions and gaps" section of `vault-local-only-binding.md` now says the headless gate decides on provider ID alone. Both parsers validate entries with one pattern, `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$`. One invalid line invalidates the whole list, so nothing is local.
4. **Path and stat parity.** The plugin resolves `env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME || resolve(env.HOME || homedir(), ".config")` from the launch env. The shell helper uses `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}` with `[[ ! -L ]]`/`[[ -f ]]` and a single portable `stat` call for mode, owner and size. GNU `stat -c` runs first, because GNU `stat -f` is file-system mode and can print unrelated output before failing. The helper is Bash 3.2 compatible.

## Behaviour

| Override state | Interactive plugin | Headless helper |
|---|---|---|
| Absent (`ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR`) | shared list (unchanged) | shared list (unchanged) |
| Valid `0600` file | only listed IDs, still loopback-only | only listed IDs |
| Insecure mode, symlink, oversized, unreadable or invalid ID | nothing is local | nothing is local |

The plugin still reads the list once at init and freezes it. The policy now also exposes `localProvidersSource` (`shared` / `operator` / `operator-invalid`) for diagnostics. The loopback endpoint check is unchanged.

## Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/local-only-policy.mjs`: override resolution, shared stat check, ID validation
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/private-processing-policy.mjs`: imports the shared check; mutation/shell refusal covers the override
- `.agents/scripts/vault-data-policy-helper.sh`: same resolution, trust check and validation
- `.agents/configs/local-ai-providers.conf`: header documents the override
- `.agents/reference/vault-local-only-binding.md`: override section and headless trust gap
- Tests: `test-local-only-policy.mjs`, `test-private-processing-policy.mjs`, `test-vault-data-policy-routing.sh`

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-local-only-policy.mjs`: 22/22 pass. New cases: absent, valid, `0644`, `0620`, symlink, invalid ID and oversized overrides, plus XDG precedence and frozen-after-load. JS and headless-helper parity is checked for each case, and the real plugin factory gets a sentinel test: a `0600` override allows `custom-local` at `http://127.0.0.1:8765` and denies `ollama`, and a `0644` copy denies everything.
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-private-processing-policy.mjs`: 7/7 pass (new override write-protection case).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-vault-data-policy-routing.sh`: 14/14 pass. It is now hermetic against the developer's own override.
- The same allow/deny matrix was checked under macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.57.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the helper and its test. `tsc --noEmit` and `markdownlint` pass. `test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh` and `test-headless-routing-retry.sh` pass.
- Not run: `setup.sh --non-interactive` against the live install, because it would deploy unmerged code. The override is resolved only from `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and never from the bundle path, so a bundle replacement cannot affect it.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. Without an override file, behaviour is the same as today.
