title: fix(worktrees): reconcile recorded owner process generations
body:
## Summary

- Reconcile each recorded owner launch by boot UUID, PID and process-start identity, preserving completed launches instead of repeatedly polling them or treating lock expiry as completion.
- Persist reconciliation through the existing registry transaction during owner admission, explicit per-worktree reconciliation and the bounded rotating lifecycle reconciliation batch.
- Keep active and unknown launches distinct. Source identity and admission epochs remain required; process completion alone never grants removal authority.
- Preserve the managed user-service completion contract. Legacy observation-only launches can supply a separate descendant-completion receipt after their recorded boot has ended, not merely because an arbitrary cgroup disappeared or changed generation.

## Implementation context

`worktree_lifetime_reconcile.py` owns durable process-completion receipts and their validation. Integration follows the existing registry writer, admission fencing and proof patterns in `worktree_lifetime_owner.py`, `worktree-managed-lifetime.py`, `worktree_lifecycle_status.py` and `worktree_lifetime_proof.py`. Operator guidance lives in `reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md`; CWD diagnostics remain a legacy fallback, not the process reconciliation mechanism.

This does not retroactively declare same-boot observation-only launches safe, stop services, require administrative access, weaken archive verification, or change retention policy.

## Verification

- Existing owner-lifetime suite: 25 tests, two environment-dependent skips.
- Focused coverage includes multiple launches, cached finished history, changed admission, PID reuse, access denial, previous boot, invalid receipts and sealed-generation proof validation.

Changelog

Changelog

Release notes for OpenCode V2, newest first.

v2.2.0 — 2026-10-27

Highlights

  • Create, install and share Desktop plugins (experimental) (#55246, #59469, #59489)
  • Refreshed the desktop app experience (#56898, #58865, #55838, #57962)
  • Add experimental image and decision generation APIs to plugins and sdk, allowing image generation or decision model (think typesafe, clef, etc) workflows. (#59190, #59380, #58758)
  • Plugins can now attach and update keyed session instructions with ctx.session.instructions.entry.put/list/remove. Instead of editing the system prompt and busting the prompt cache, each change is added as a small update at the next step. The entries also survive compaction and reverts, and they don't start an extra model turn. (#56550)
  • Restored the Todo tool in desktop via opt-in (#59092)
  • Add configurable prompt cache TTLs per provider/model (#59157)

Breaking changes

@opencode/ai root is now the Promise API

@opencode/ai now works like @opencode/sdk and @opencode/client: the package root exports the Promise API, and the Effect API moved to @opencode/ai/effect. @opencode/ai/promise is removed, and the wildcard subpath export is replaced with an explicit list of provider and protocol entry points. (#58847, #59183)

-import { AI } from "@opencode/ai/promise"
-import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai"
+import { AI } from "@opencode/ai"
+import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai/effect"

The OpenCode GitHub Action is removed

The OpenCode GitHub Action is no longer published. Remove it from your workflows. (#59032)

TUI plugins require OpenTUI 0.7

@opencode/plugin now requires @opentui/core and @opentui/solid 0.7.0, up from 0.6.8 or later. Plugins that depend on OpenTUI 0.6 fail to install until they upgrade. In OpenTUI 0.7, custom renderables read their hooks from their class at construction: assign renderBefore, renderAfter, and onLifecyclePass in the constructor instead of as class fields, call refreshHooks() after adding a hook by reflection, and replace defineNativeIntegration() with a static nativeIntegration declaration. See the OpenTUI 0.7.0 release notes. (#59295)

Core

Improvements

  • Add experimental image and decision generation API endpoints. (#59190)
  • Add image and decision entrypoints for catalog providers. (#59380)
  • Improve integration rebuild performance. (#59402)
  • Let custom model configuration set a model type. (#59388)
  • Let model-list API requests filter by type. (#59355)
  • Make external-directory permission checks use the project's filesystem. (#59089)
  • Reduce memory use when code search finds very large lines. (#59205)
  • Let plugins filter event subscriptions by type. (#58864)
  • Add configurable prompt-cache TTLs. (#59157)
  • Move image resizing off the main process and release idle image memory. (#58820)

Changes are scoped to `worktree-maintenance.py`, the new `worktree_maintenance_worker.py`, the existing maintenance policy adapter, shared Pulse retention predicate, branch-preservation hook, process-snapshot argument validation and the existing maintenance tests. [INFO] Wait until reset epoch 1793144448 before retrying. Re-authentication or forwarding GH_TOKEN will not help before reset.

[INFO] Retry after 2026-10-27 23:40:48 GMT local time, in about 14 min (reset epoch 1793144448). Re-authentication or forwarding GH_TOKEN will not help before reset.

title: GH#35788: fix fleet capability circuit and checkpoint remediation
body:
## Summary

Resolves #35788.

- Hold redispatch after two distinct authenticated runners report the same capability blocker for the same task revision. A single runner remains a runner-local failure.
- Upsert one repository supervisor escalation, retain observed issue lists, and reconcile concurrent duplicate creators without deleting ordinary or untrusted dashboard comments.
- Probe readiness before worker launch. Bind shared wake receipts to the exact issue revision and failed observation IDs, not a class-wide fingerprint or runner clocks.
- Invalidate local capability cooldowns when the approved policy or installed-tool readiness changes.
- Give capability checkpoint owners concrete runner remediation rather than instructions to revise the brief or discard the checkpoint.

The lockfile-policy portion was already implemented in merged #35797; this PR reuses it rather than duplicating that change.

## Files and reference patterns

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: existing trusted observation markers, task revisions, and shared dispatch gate; new fleet aggregation, readiness, supervisor escalation, and duplicate reconciliation.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`: existing runner-local cooldown configuration fingerprint, extended with policy and tool readiness wake signals.
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: existing blocked checkpoint attention path, with capability-specific remediation text.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: existing regression harness, extended for distinct runners, forged/untrusted evidence, revision changes, exact-checkpoint wake receipts, escalation upserts, duplicate reconciliation, and capability attention.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high. Testing: runtime-verified.

Implementation head: `1119ea9960b357cb56b44b192f875d3488c56b18`.

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: **42 tests, 0 failures**, including a fresh run on the final implementation commit.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-js-dependency-bootstrap.sh`: **36 passing assertions**.
- `shellcheck` on all four changed shell files: passed.
- `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main --head HEAD`: passed, zero new violations.
- `bun run typecheck`: passed through the pre-push gate on the final pushed head.
- Focused fleet and checkpoint cases passed again after integrating the current default branch.

Additional verification found a **pre-existing** failure in `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: the blocked-attention fixture reports `boolean (true) cannot be matched, as it is not a string` before reaching the changed text branch. Reproducing the unchanged test prefix with the `origin/main` helper source produced the same failure (**40 tests, 1 failure**). That unrelated classifier/test defect is reported here and is not repaired in this PR.

## Design decisions and review

- Keep normal issue eligibility available so a new capable runner can perform the prelaunch probe; immutable shared releases and the supervisor record supply the durable fleet circuit rather than a label that would prevent readiness checks.
- The existing capability fingerprint identifies a blocker class. Scope readiness receipts by task revision and server observation IDs so one task's readiness cannot clear another task or a later failure.
- GitHub comments have no atomic upsert. Concurrent creators converge through trusted duplicate reconciliation; subsequent observations edit the canonical comment.
- No implicit dependency installation, permission change, hook bypass, or approval bypass is introduced.
- Independent closeout review found no material defects. Review bundle: `52b21c8ab8cab4d0747b1f2fdf8a89a69fde53ed37aa237462ad39b5904e5a98` (injection scan clean).

title: GH#35842: fix atomic worker lifecycle launch registration
body:
## Summary

Resolves #35842. Follow-up to #35826; Ref #35821.

- Commit pre-exec process registration and its initial hypothetical worktree binding in one transaction in the existing `registry.sqlite3`.
- Reuse the existing event formats, deduplication and schema 1. Stable UUIDv5 event keys derived from the run UUID make exact attempt retries idempotent; conflicting payloads fail without changing existing evidence.
- Resolve the worktree path before the write transaction. A binding error or insufficient journal capacity now leaves no partial registered run. Preserve observe-only fail-open native command behavior.
- Replace the existing registry zipapp and its two native reports with the identical artifact tested on Linux and macOS. Process artifacts are unchanged; exactly two zipapps and four reports remain.

## Files and reference pattern

Production changes are limited to `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/{store,launch}.py`, using the existing `connection(write=True)` transaction and `_event` deduplication pattern. Existing `tests/test_store.py` and `tests/test_launch.py` cover rollback, exact/conflicting/concurrent replay and owned-process crashes. `REGISTRY.md` and `COMPATIBILITY.md` describe the contract and evidence; the existing registry artifact/reports retain their established filenames.

## Runtime testing

- Source suite: 41 tests pass.
- Fresh standalone registry bundle: 30 tests pass on Linux 6.18.55 x86-64, Python 3.13.15, SQLite 3.51.2.
- Operator-returned native macOS report: the same 30 tests pass on Darwin 21.6.0 x86-64, Python 3.14.6, SQLite 3.53.3. No failures or skips on either host.
- Both reports match the checked-in artifact SHA-256: `7d0e97ca383e41b97d4ecbbc17ded633a1e451b600980e99f4d021fac7b0771e`.
- Actual owned subprocesses crash after both SQL writes but before commit, and after commit before acknowledgement. Reopen/replay checks verify no partial state or duplicate pair. Concurrent retries and replay after an ended observation also pass.
- Existing sandbox command-policy suite: 57/57. Ruff 0.11.13, mypy 1.15.0 for Linux and Darwin, and diff checks pass. Darwin type checking is separate from the native macOS execution above.

## Regression Evidence

Automated regression coverage is present; no testing exemption is requested. The platform-fix gate's path recognizer does not recognize this package's existing test directory. This PR changes `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_store.py` and `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_launch.py`, executed by the scoped Python CI job and by the standalone registry validator.

The real native launcher capacity regression now requires zero persisted events, runs and bindings when only one journal slot remains; the former two-transaction implementation left a partial registered run. Added tests exercise concurrent exact replay, conflicting binding rollback, replay after termination, and owned-process crashes before and after commit. The existing source suite passes 41 tests. The checked-in registry bundle passes 30 tests on both Linux and native macOS with matching report fingerprints. A duplicate shell regression is not appropriate for this Python/SQLite transaction change; the automated tests reside beside the package they exercise.

## Risk and limits

Risk: medium. Testing: runtime-verified for the stated disposable native-process/SQLite scenarios, not production AI workers.

No new database, broker, outbox, scheduler, schema migration or cleanup authority. `cleanup_authorized` remains false and legacy state is untouched. A committed attempt does not prove exec success, application readiness or descendant quiescence. The wrapper allocates a fresh run ID per invocation; this is store-level idempotency, not durable delivery when storage is unavailable. SQLite and exec are not one atomic operation. Power loss, disk full, reboot, real PID reuse, real AI workers and macOS sandbox launch remain outside this evidence.

Rollback: revert these commits; existing schema/event records need no migration or reset.

- Expand literal `~/` configuration prefixes consistently across both launchers and Pulse. Unchanged observations advance only concurrency/rotation metadata; first observations, changed results and terminal transitions remain journaled without consuming capacity on every idle tick.
- Prepare the framework workspace in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh` before runtime-bundle activation. Create only the parent, preserve existing state, and expose its canonical path to later setup steps; private registry creation remains the first worker's responsibility.

- Sandbox command-policy suite: 61 checks passed (`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-command-policy.sh`), including default activation, opt-out, private-workload exclusion and literal home-prefix configuration.
- Pulse cycle-gate suite: 60 checks passed (`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh`), including a real native launch transitioning to `ended` through the Pulse hook, timeout containment, opt-out/diagnostic guards, unknown-state preservation and entry-point ordering.

title: GH#35855: publish Cloudron catalog with the job token; PAT only when main rules block it
body:
## Summary

The managed Cloudron catalog workflow now pushes its catalog commit and tag with the per-run job token by default. `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` stays an optional override. It is required only when rules on `main` block a direct job-token push: required PRs, status checks or deployments, or restricted updates.

Resolves #35855

## Why

Per-repository PATs were a manual setup and rotation cost that protected nothing:

- Every package repo has only the baseline rules, `non_fast_forward` and `deletion`. Neither blocks a fast-forward push by `github-actions[bot]`.
- The pre-migration inline workflows already pushed with `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT || github.token`. nostr-relay 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 were published that way.
- nostr-relay 0.1.2 (run 40440804288) failed only because the reusable workflow hard-required the PAT.

The job token is scoped to the one repository and expires with the job, which is narrower than any PAT. Only the final push step receives it; the npm/CLI steps get no token in their environment.

## Changes

- `cloudron-catalog-publish-reusable.yml`: `publish` gets `contents: write`, and the push uses `secrets.CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT || github.token`. The trust-boundary marker is kept on the push.
- `cloudron-package-release-lib.sh`: new `cloudron_publication_pat_required`, which reads `rules/branches/main` and returns 0 (required), 1 (not required) or 2 (unreadable).
- The approval, scaffold and monitor helpers check the secret only when that function says it's required. Unreadable rules still fail closed for approvals and the monitor.
- Docs and the caller template describe the job-token default. For owners who adopt required-PR rules, the docs say one multi-repo PAT is enough.

## Rollout

Permission rollout named for the reusable-permission gate:

`aidevops sync-workflows --apply --workflow cloudron-catalog-publish`

Callers need no permission change. All 7 live callers already grant `contents: write` (checked 2026-10-29 on the `main` branch of each package repository), so the job-level grant stays within what callers give.

Callers pin an immutable SHA, so the change takes effect per repository only when its pin moves to this PR's merge commit. Order:

1. nostr-relay: publishes the signed 0.1.2 release, blocked since run 40440804288.
2. headscale and opendesk: no PAT secret, so their next release would fail the same way.
3. The other four have a PAT and can converge with routine pin updates.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on 7 changed scripts: clean. `actionlint` on the workflow: clean.
- `test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` passes, including new `rules_error`, `pat_present` and baseline no-secret-lookup cases.
- `test-cloudron-package-init.sh`: 45/45, including baseline (no warning), unreadable rules, required plus missing, and required plus present.
- `test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh` passes; the workflow push-script race test now uses `PUSH_TOKEN`.
- `test-cloudron-release-evidence.py`: 19/19.
- `linters-local.sh --changed`: passes. shfmt advisories are pre-existing lines outside this diff.
- Live: after merge, bump nostr-relay's caller pin; the push to main should publish 0.1.2 with no PAT.

title: GH#35871: stop stranded-commit, salvage and review-route issue loops
body:
## Summary

Fixes the root causes that kept worker issues looping and accumulating lifecycle comments without ever delivering.

| Root cause | Evidence | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Typecheck ran only in the local pre-push hook, never in CI. Worker worktrees without `tsc` exited 127, so committed work never left the runner that made it. | #35689 and #35751 brief histories. Checkpoints `0454795df`, `748b04f50`, `6cdde1f8f` and `0519aac6a` return HTTP 422 on GitHub. | NEW `.github/workflows/typecheck.yml`. The hook now defers a typecheck that cannot start for missing dev dependencies, but only when the remote default branch's CI runs the identical command. It reads the remote-tracking ref, never the pushed tree. Real type errors still block. |
| Consolidation made "salvage these exact commits; do not recreate" binding, so every other runner exited BLOCKED forever. | 139 and 116 comments. The #23126 fleet dashboard re-woke the same blocker 5 times. | Worker prompt (first-pass item 1) and consolidation constraints: a checkpoint that no remote ref holds is best-effort, and the spec is the source of truth. The recovery supervisor may rewrite such briefs. |
| Not-reproduced investigations waited on a maintainer closeout. | #35194 supervisor decision, 2026-10-23 | `worker-discipline.md` lets the supervisor close them after 72h without recurrence once diagnostics have merged. |
| The review-thread remediation suite pointed at a moved sub-library, ran 0 cases and still exited 0. | `Tests run: 0` on `main` | Path fixed; it now runs 27 cases. |

**Deliberately not changed:** `CHANGES_REQUESTED` remediation-first stays opt-in. CodeRabbit still files formal change requests on branches cut before GH#35860; #35872 got one at 00:42, after GH#35860 merged at 00:38. With remediation-first as the default, such a PR converges and then keeps `preserving the review block` (`pulse-merge.sh` converged branch) forever, because nothing dismisses an advisory bot review there. The legacy route churns at most once, then lands on a post-GH#35860 branch. #35867 (already queued) adds the defence in depth: it stops routing and dismisses bot-only change requests. Flipping the default is only worth revisiting after that lands.

## Summary

Resolves #35881

- Add timeline-backed suppression for protected-label removals that reverse the scanner identity's own add within 24 hours, with no intervening actor.

| Foreign actor retains alert | `foreign_add`, `foreign_remove`, `intervening`, `foreign_readd` cases |
| API failure retains alert | `api_error`, `user_error`, `malformed`, `truncated` cases |
| Additional signals retain alert | `mixed`, `capture`, `multiple` cases |
| Existing expected transitions still pass | Complete existing regression script passes |
| ShellCheck zero findings | Local executable unavailable; remote cross-platform ShellCheck remains authoritative |

Direct diff review plus bounded independent advisory review found a latest-add race, repaired in the second commit and verified by `readd`, `foreign_readd`, and `future_readd` cases. Timeline pagination uses explicit page requests rather than unbounded `--paginate`, so the five-page cap is enforced. A full fifth page is treated as potentially truncated and retains the alert. A conservative timestamp window prevents an older add/remove cycle from hiding an unmatched removal.

title: GH#35896: keep secret run stdout/stderr separate so MCP stdio responses are not corrupted
body:
## Summary

aidevops secret NAME -- cmd and secret run merged the child's stderr into stdout (2>&1) before redaction. Pipe writes above PIPE_BUF are not atomic, so stderr log lines from concurrent requests landed inside large chunked JSON-RPC responses, corrupting them; MCP clients dropped the lines and timed out. Both run paths now share run_with_redacted_streams: stdout keeps its redactor, stderr gets its own redactor via a private FIFO back to fd 2 (waitable on Bash 3.2), stdin is inherited, exit codes preserved. The second relay runs quiet so short-value warnings are not duplicated. No new --exec flag: the default launcher is now transparent and keeps redaction on both streams.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/secret-handling.md, .agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — Deterministic fixture (stdio server writing ~200 KB responses in 8 KB chunks while concurrent requests log to stderr; 6 concurrent requests, parent stderr unread): before 4/6 received with 8 non-JSON lines, both large responses lost; after 6/6 with 0 non-JSON lines, with parent stderr read or unread, under bash 5 and /bin/bash 3.2. Throughput unchanged (360 KB in 0.53 s, byte-identical). secret run and NAME -- paths: stdout and stderr each [REDACTED], exit code 7 preserved. test-secret-helper.sh 47/47 (bash 5 and 3.2), test-secret-resolver.sh 14/14, ShellCheck clean. test-runner-capability.sh fails identically on unmodified main (pre-existing, unrelated).

Executed existing offline verifier/attestation suite through `CatalogEvidence.verify()`, including direct-parent compatibility and docs-only acceptance. The original private release cannot be replayed: its repository and PR identity are omitted from the brief. No production receipt was mutated or claimed verified.

Independent read-only review found a first-parent-only merge-diff gap; fixed by rejecting intervening merges, then reviewer verified resolution. Accept complete linear histories of at most 250 intervening commits with fewer than 100 files per commit; reject merges because REST diffs do not prove every parent. These limits fail closed and are documented.

title: GH#35883: fix: count capability releases as one stall and let capable runners continue the head
body:
## Summary

`runner_capability_unmet` releases describe the releasing runner, not the draft head. `_pcc_stall_release_evidence` counted each one as a stall, so two runners without the capability used up the two-stall exact-head budget, attention was posted, and no capable runner ever tried the head. The successor worker's fence also accepted a capability release only while the issue was still released. After the continuation claimed the issue, the fence ran with the issue assigned and rejected every capability continuation before launch. Drafts #35598 and #35603 show the deadlock.

- All capability releases since the head count once, as the original stall. Each genuine stall still counts on its own, so one genuine stall after capability releases still posts attention.
- New `_pcc_self_capability_release`: a runner skips a head that its own login released for a missing capability, with no comment and no dispatch, so another runner can continue it. A newer standalone OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` re-arms the runner; quoted text and circuit-record text do not. A new head re-arms every runner.
- `_pr_checkpoint_issue_metadata_is_eligible`: the capability-class exception now also applies after ownership transfers. Ordinary `blocked` releases still need `CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_APPROVED`. Assignment, lifecycle and protective-label checks are unchanged.
- `epoch`, `release_reason` and `blocked_release` move into the shared jq defs.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh, .agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium (dispatch eligibility for released drafts)
- **Verification:** self-assessed.
  - `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` passes 106/106 under jq 1.7.1, the version CI uses. New cases cover: aggregate capability releases; per-runner skip with no comment or dispatch; trusted retry, plus quoted and untrusted retries that must not re-arm; new-head re-arm; the genuine-stall threshold; and the transferred-worker fence, with ordinary blocked releases still fenced.
  - Under jq 1.8.2 the suite fails at the same pre-existing case on unmodified `main`. That is a separate binding-precedence bug, tracked in #35920.

title: GH#35920: fix(jq): portable binding precedence for jq 1.7/1.8 and a blocking gate
body:
## Summary

jq 1.8 changed binding precedence (jqlang/jq #3053, #3326). `blocked_by_runner` in `_pcc_blocked_release_evidence` bound the release line with `as` after `and`. jq 1.8.2 groups that as `(A and T) as $line`, so the variable held a boolean and every call failed with `boolean (true) cannot be matched, as it is not a string`. The caller reads that failure as "no blocked release", so runners with Homebrew jq 1.8 first on PATH (the launchd default) never posted blocked-checkpoint attention. CI and macOS `/usr/bin/jq` run jq 1.7.1, which groups the program as intended, so every test stayed green.

- `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: `blocked_by_runner` pipes the release line straight into its comparisons, with no binding.
- New `.agents/scripts/jq-binding-precedence-check.py`: rejects a binding after an operator (`and`, `or`, comparisons, arithmetic, `//`, assignment operators, `try`, `catch`) in `.sh`, `.bash`, `.jq`, `.py`, `.yml` and `.yaml` files and in extensionless shell or Python scripts. A one-line override needs a stated reason. After the fix the whole tracked tree is clean.
- Blocking gate with a zero baseline in `linters-local.sh` (full and `--changed`) and in the CI `Complexity Analysis` job.
- `reference/shell-style-guide.md`: a jq 1.7/1.8 portability section with the banned form, both explicit forms, and other divergences checked under both versions (guidance, not gated).

### Bundled: #35932, capability-release attention

`_pcc_blocked_attention` checked for a `runner_capability_unmet` release with `any(.[]; .id == …)`, but `_pcc_issue_comments` returns `gh api --paginate --slurp` pages. `.[]` yielded page arrays, jq failed with `Cannot index array with string "id"`, and every capability release got the brief-owner body, which asks a human to edit the brief for a runner prerequisite. The check now iterates `flatten[]`, like every other evidence query in the helper. The test stub in `test_capability_checkpoint_attention` returned a flat array that production never produces; it now returns pages, and with that fixture unmodified `main` fails the test.

It ships here because of ordering. Once the jq 1.8 fix lands, jq 1.8 runners start posting blocked attention on the drafts that were silently stalled, and without #35932 each capability release among them would get the wrong body.

## Files Changed

.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md, .agents/scripts/jq-binding-precedence-check.py, .agents/scripts/lint-file-discovery.sh, .agents/scripts/linters-local-analysis.sh, .agents/scripts/linters-local-gates.sh, .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-jq-binding-precedence-check.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh, .github/workflows/code-quality.yml

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** self-assessed — unit suites under both jq versions, plus lint gates.
  - `test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: 94/94 under jq 1.7.1 (`/usr/bin/jq`) and 94/94 under jq 1.8.2 (`/opt/homebrew/bin/jq`), with no `jq: error` lines on stderr after #35932. Unmodified `main` fails under jq 1.8.2 (reproducer in #35920).
  - `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: 42/42. With the paginated fixture and the old query, `capability checkpoint attention names runner remediation, not a brief revision` fails with the production error.
  - `test-jq-binding-precedence-check.sh`: 69/69, covering each operator, each file type, the override, and false-positive shapes.
  - `git ls-files | python3 .agents/scripts/jq-binding-precedence-check.py -`: no findings, rechecked after rebasing onto current `main`.
  - `linters-local.sh --changed`: all local checks passed, including ShellCheck and the new gate; actionlint accepts the workflow.

title: GH#35935: make dispatch-stage report honour its window and bound the log
body:
## Summary

`dispatch-stage-instrument.sh report [window_s]` now honours its window and finishes in seconds on a log holding months of records. The pulse now trims `dispatch-stages.tsv` every cycle and removes scratch copies that killed reports left behind.

## Why

On the maintainer runner the stage log had grown to 200 MB and 1.9M lines (six months). `report 86400` timed out at 60 s, and a 7-day report was killed at 300 s with no output. The causes:

- `_ds_report` copied the whole log line by line in Bash into `${DS_LOG}.report.*`. The awk then kept every sample and insertion-sorted each stage, which is O(n²).
- The awk ignored `cutoff` ("currently unused"), so the "last 24h" report covered all time.
- Nothing in production called `_ds_trim_log`; only the manual `trim` subcommand did.
- Killed reports left log-sized scratch copies behind (about 749 MB across six files).

As a result, #35605 had been blocked on a precondition (`report 86400`) that could not complete on the runner that held its data.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-stage-instrument.sh`
  - `_ds_report`: one awk pass filters the window by ISO-8601 UTC string comparison and skips `start` rows. A `LC_ALL=C sort` follows, then an O(n) percentile pass. No scratch copy is written. A non-numeric window is rejected with an error.
  - `_ds_epoch_to_iso`: portable epoch → ISO formatting (GNU `-d @N`, BSD `-r N`).
  - `_ds_trim_log`: writes to `${DS_LOG}.trim.*`, falls back to the default when the cap is invalid, and removes the temp file on failure. Each run also calls `_ds_cleanup_stale_temp`, which deletes `.report.*` / `.trim.*` files older than 60 minutes.
  - The default `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_STAGES_LOG_MAX_LINES` rises from 50000 to 200000 (about 16 days at ~12.5k records/day), so 7-day reports keep their data.
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-stage-aggregate.awk`: adds `mode=filter` and `mode=aggregate` (the default) over the pre-sorted stream. Percentile indexes are unchanged, and output rows are sorted by stage.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh`: `_pulse_efficiency_cycle_finish` calls `_ds_trim_log` next to `gh_trim_log`. The pulse already sources the instrument through `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`.
- `.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md`: documents the window, the automatic trim, the cleanup and the new default, and fixes the manual p95 snippet so it skips `start` rows.

Other log readers (`pulse-current-state.py` `recent_lines`, `circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh`, `stats-health-dashboard-data.sh`) read only recent rows and keep no file offsets, so rotation is safe for them.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` is clean on both changed scripts, `markdownlint` is clean on the doc, and the pre-commit and pre-push gates passed.
- Real data (static copy of the 1.9M-line log): `report 86400` ran in 3.9 s, down from more than 60 s. `precreate.helper_add` gave n=62, p50 26340, p95 81331, p99 181858, max 234371. An independent awk + `sort -n` run over the same window gave the same values. `dedup.worker_spawn` (57) and `dedup.gh_issue_view` (449) counts also match. `report 604800` ran in 3.8 s.
- Window check on a synthetic log: `report 3600` excludes a 30-day-old row, `start` rows, zero-elapsed rows and rows with an `unknown` timestamp. `report 8640000` includes the old row. `report 1h` is rejected.
- Trim on the copy: 1.9M lines down to 100000 in 0.27 s. Stale `.report.*` / `.trim.*` files were removed and fresh and unrelated files kept. `_ds_record` still appends after the trim, and a trim below the cap leaves the log untouched.
- Existing suites pass: `test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh` (6/6), `test-stats-worker-zero-diagnostics.sh` (4/4), `test-pulse-current-state-helper.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh` (60/60) and `test-fix-the-fixer-observability.sh` (34/34).

## Follow-up

With the report working, #35605's evidence threshold is met on the maintainer runner: 62 `precreate.helper_add` records in 24 h and 280 in 7 d (the brief asks for about 30). #35605 can be re-evaluated for dispatch once this is deployed.

Resolves #35935

title: t18790: keep Task-ID Collision Guard CI history complete
body:
## Summary

The Task-ID Collision Guard workflow checked out full history, then refetched main, develop and task-id-counter with --depth=100. A depth-limited fetch into a complete clone writes .git/shallow, so the guard's git log --all stopped about 100 claims behind the counter tip and properly claimed task IDs failed as unclaimed (t18514 on PR #35946; t18403/t18405/t18407 on GH#33881). Pulse treats that unclassified red check as a merge blocker. The workflow now refetches without --depth and unshallows a shallow checkout; the guard warns instead of blocking when a shallow repository hides the claim for an at-or-below-counter ID. IDs above the counter and never-claimed IDs in full history still block.



## Files Changed

.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh, .github/workflows/task-id-collision-check.yml

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime-verified with synthetic origin/clone repositories driving the real guard and the real workflow step (scripts kept out of the repo). The fixture counter is 10; "old claim" is an ID claimed 150 commits behind the counter-branch tip, "never claimed" is an ID at or below the counter with no claim commit, and "invented" is an ID above the counter.

- Workflow fetch step (extracted verbatim from the YAML and executed): old step on a full clone -> `shallow=true`, 100 counter-branch commits, old claim hidden; new step on a full clone -> `shallow=false`, 151 commits, old claim visible; new step on a `--depth=1` clone -> warns, unshallows -> `shallow=false`, 151 commits, old claim visible.

title: GH#35975: fix: bound secret-run stderr backpressure
body:
## Summary
Prevent an unread parent stderr pipe from stalling secret-run children. The FIFO still redacts stderr independently; a bounded best-effort sink drains it without contaminating lossless stdout.

Resolves #35975

## Files and reference
- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`: extend the existing FIFO/redactor pipeline with a bounded queue and daemon writer; verify Python exists before launching the child.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh`: extend the isolated runtime suite with saturated unread stderr for specific-secret, run-all, and no-usable-redaction-value paths.

## Runtime Testing
- Risk: critical (credential redaction); testing: runtime-verified.
- Exact head: `9d2ce76675f69ab43b6e5893ff844001d972b8fe`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh`: **48 passed, 0 failed** on the final committed head.
- Saturation regression confirms child progress, interactive stdin, separate stdout, redacted stderr, and exit status 23 without reading stderr until after child exit.
- `bash -n` on both modified scripts and `git diff --check`: passed; pre-commit and pre-push hooks passed.
- ShellCheck executable wrapper has no real binary; no worktree-local binary or .aidevops.json declaration exists. Covered remotely by `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` cross-platform-shellcheck.
- Push wrapper defers root TypeScript typecheck to CI because tsc/dev dependencies are absent; this PR changes shell/Python only.

## Trade-offs and review
Only redacted diagnostics enter the queue (16 x 64 KiB). Excess diagnostics are dropped under backpressure; at EOF the writer gets 250 ms to drain, so stderr is intentionally best-effort. Stdout is never dropped. Inherited fd flags are unchanged, and no plaintext diagnostic spool is created.

Independent focused review identified the missing Python preflight; fixed before final verification. No other introduced defect was identified. Direct final diff and acceptance review verified all functional criteria above. The review-bundle command could not run because the runner lacks the `file` utility; the exact patch was reviewed directly.

## Acceptance
| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unread stderr cannot stall child | satisfied | Saturation tests across all three modes |
| Redaction and stream separation | satisfied | Saturation plus existing literal, overlap, and streaming tests |
| Preserve stdin and exit status | satisfied | READY/continue/DONE handshake, exit 23 |
| Bounded diagnostics without shared flag mutations | satisfied | Bounded queue, daemon writer and bounded join |

body:
## Summary

Resolves #35996.

Adds staged worktree generation enrollment and admission, replacing closed PR #35966. This branch excludes the parallel contributions added to that previous PR.

The owner requests review and merge once gates pass. Review feedback is welcome in comments; please do not commit directly to this branch. Deployment, production database migration and cleanup activation are not requested.

## Implementation and review context

- Primary files: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/{storage,admission,enrollment,launch,directory_handle,cleanup_policy}.py` and `.agents/scripts/{shared-worktree-create,worker-lifecycle-state,headless-runtime-invoke,sandbox-exec-helper}.sh`.
- Adds transactional admission, restartable generation registration, native launch integration, and report-only cleanup decisions. Uses existing `LifecycleRegistry` event/projection transactions and the `worker-launch.py` exec path.
- Archive administration excludes runtime generation markers so restored worktrees receive new identities rather than inheriting the source marker. Existing symlink rejection remains enabled.
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md` documents rollout boundaries. `cleanup_authorized` remains false; the legacy mechanism is not retired.

## Runtime Testing

- Risk: high (admission and lifecycle boundaries). Linux disposable-Git/process/SQLite tests exercise the production CLI and creation hook; no production state is migrated or deleted.
- Lifecycle unit/integration suite: 114 passing tests, including schema-1 compatibility, conflicting marker/table refusal, failure diagnostics, missing/replaced registered paths, canonical aliases and closed admission.
- Profile boundary suite: 28 passing tests.
- Portable registry validator: 71 passing tests on Linux for bundle `bd629a78c7f286018d4ba3188a2e494812c3664a7eb2a588528e899ee20533fc`.
- Scoped Ruff, mypy (Linux and macOS targets), and ShellCheck passed. CI must independently pass on the published head.
- Independent current-source review covered the production admission, enrollment, launch, directory-handle, cleanup-policy, storage, shell-launch and archive contracts. Its registered-path resolution finding was repaired and re-reviewed; no remaining finding was reported. This was static source review, not an independent test run or verified full-diff review.
- The macOS report describes an earlier artifact; current enrollment integration remains unqualified on macOS.

## Reviewed safeguards

- Python annotation compatibility, deterministic Git test environment, preserved enrollment error JSON, and consistent staged-admission documentation.
- Marker format 2 persists inode identity rather than unstable device numbers. Format-1 compatibility does not rewrite metadata or reopen closed admission; operation-local device checks remain. Simulated renumbering is not native reboot/remount qualification.
- Schema-1 creation stays observe-only with an explicit coverage-gap diagnostic; it does not silently migrate or claim admission. Markers or admission tables in schema 1 are refused. Ordinary enrollment remains strict.
- Registered declared paths are checked before symlink resolution. Missing or replaced paths fail closed, and the selected canonical path is passed directly into admitted launch without another unguarded resolution.
- Narrow Semgrep false-positive explanations cover the fixed Git argv call and SQLite PRAGMA interpolation of module integer constants. No untrusted SQL input, shell interpolation, global suppression or scan configuration change is introduced.

## Remaining rollout boundaries

Existing schema-1 installations require a coordinated migration before mandatory admission. Complete writer/session/descendant coverage is still absent. Process termination and generation identity do not authorize deletion. The explicit remaining-boundary table in `CLEANUP.md` is the continuation plan; this PR does not claim full retirement of legacy ownership or production cleanup readiness.

## Summary

Resolves #35993 (t18794).

- After successfully posting a terminal dispatch lease, minimize that runner's finished-attempt claim, lease and dispatch comments as `OUTDATED`.

- Use one bounded GraphQL comment query, skip already-minimized comments and low GraphQL budgets, stop on failures, and cap best-effort hygiene to five seconds without changing terminal transition success.

## Files and reference

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh`: terminal transition integration and private best-effort minimization function.
- Reference: `.agents/scripts/stats-quality-sweep-issues.sh` `minimizeComment` / `OUTDATED` pattern.
- Existing dispatch producers already include the required lease identity and attempt ID; parser payloads are neither edited nor deleted.

- `bash -n .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh` passed.
- Focused isolated fixture checks passed: exact attempt selection, peer/live/release/blocker preservation, already-minimized exclusion, low budget, mutation failure, partial GraphQL errors, and an actual stalled-process timeout returning success within the five-second hygiene budget.
- `test-dispatch-lifecycle-comms.sh`: 25 passed, 0 failed.
- `test-dispatch-atomic-lease.sh`: passed, including ready-handoff terminal release and exact-generation concurrency checks.
- `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: 43 passed, 0 failed.

Both failures reproduce identically on the unchanged base `b80656f55` (104 tests, 2 failures): `claim POST fallback pre-creates private stderr file` and `claim POST fallback creates file under restrictive umask`. The failure evidence reports a directory mode rather than the expected private stderr-file mode. This PR does not change claim posting or these assertions.
- The existing authenticated-generation lease-parser fixture gives identical output with every comment's `isMinimized` toggled false/true. Exact searches find no `isMinimized` filtering in `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`, `pr_checkpoint_events.py`, or `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`.

- Authenticated GraphQL query works on #35993. Its only dispatch attempt is still live and remains unminimized; a real post-terminal mutation must be observed after rollout rather than prematurely terminating the active worker lease. No live minimization result is claimed.

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — production terminal transition exercised by the atomic-lease suite; production minimization function exercised with isolated GitHub responses and real process timeout; existing lease parser tested against minimized and visible comments. Live post-rollout validation remains as noted above.

## Boundaries

No comment deletion or body editing; no parser or ownership-protocol changes. Hygiene only scans the latest 100 comments and defers when the terminal marker is absent, GraphQL reserve is below 100 points, a bounded request fails, or the five-second deadline expires.

body:
## Summary

Resolves #35998.

Adds `record-deployment PR RUN_ID WORKFLOW.yml DEPLOYED_SHA REPO` to verify an existing tagless maintained-application deployment before finalizing cleanup. The new helper binds a successful push run to the same repository, PR base branch, immutable deployed SHA, trusted actors, latest workflow invocation and merge ancestry. Versioned publication and live-owner cleanup guards remain unchanged.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-deployment.sh`: read-only deployment verification and atomic receipt recording
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`: terminal evidence and completion integration
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-release.sh`: preserve typed evidence across shared status writes
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`: command routing/help
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh`: focused success, rejection, replay, proof-retention and finalization regressions
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`: supported invocation, deployment semantics and safety boundaries

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** high
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — production shell lifecycle commands exercised through the existing isolated GitHub/receipt regression tooling, without deploying or touching an application

Passed on exact head `923184f36321f9e6e91a9843d64f0072af35cf6e`:

- ShellCheck for all changed helpers and the changed regression script
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-authority-profiles.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh` (28/28)
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh`

The pre-push repository verifier reports `tsc` unavailable because JavaScript dev dependencies are not installed. Its configured CI equivalent covers `bun run typecheck`; no TypeScript or package configuration changed.

## Decisions and review

The caller explicitly selects the deployment workflow and supplies the full SHA observed at the deployed runtime; build-only workflows and health-only evidence are not valid deployment proof. The helper verifies remote run identity and ancestry, not application-specific workflow semantics. No new application environment or JSON import is introduced.

Typed deployment proof is embedded in the same atomic status receipt. The legacy rename adapter refuses these receipts rather than discarding their repository-bound evidence. Existing versioned receipts remain single-line files; aidevops retains its signed versioned-release path.

Independent safety review findings were reproduced and repaired: strict whole-receipt framing, migration refusal, and shared-writer proof preservation, including empty payload and missing-newline corruption. Final exact-head diff inspection and acceptance matrix below are self-review.

Review bundle SHA-256: `424598db6766e08253d500e8135f8c0e13d35c6b256ca62343e1f4e9d469071d`.

## Acceptance matrix

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supported successful tagless deployment can finalize matching cleanup | Satisfied | Production recorder/finalizer regression with successful named push run, immutable SHA, trusted actors and merge ancestry |
| Missing, failed, pending, stale, unrelated or untrusted proof rejected | Satisfied | Negative regression matrix, forged JSON rejection and revalidation at finalization |
| No fabricated release, no false not-requested, no live-owner removal or extra app environment | Satisfied | Read-only GitHub API path, typed published receipt, unchanged deferred owner, live-owner regressions |
| Versioned-release and cleanup-ownership checks remain green | Satisfied | Five existing focused suites and changed-file ShellCheck pass |

No application deployment, tag, GitHub Release or data mutation is performed.
